💡 Key Takeaways
  • Elon Musk's social network X just got a new feature it never had under previous ownership.
  • That would be parental controls for teen customers, to be exact.
  • According to recent reports, these features include the ability to monitor usage and set daily limits for the teen, as well as the option to require newly introduced followers to be approved by the parent or guardian.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk's social network X just got a new feature it never had under previous ownership.

That would be parental controls for teen customers, to be exact. In a upcoming post from the official Safety account on X, the company revealed it has implemented parental controls for users aged 13 to 17. The way it works is that an account run by a parent or guardian establishes a supervisory link to the account run by a teen, which gives the parent or guardian access to a bunch of monitoring and safety features the site didn't have before.

According to recent reports, these features include the ability to monitor usage and set daily limits for the teen, as well as the option to require newly introduced followers to be approved by the parent or guardian. Recommendations on the For You feed can be limited to accounts the teen already follows, while parents can mute specific words, control who can send direct messages, and see who the teens have chatted with in DMs without seeing the messages themselves.

It has been revealed that as X noted, this only starts when both parties in the equation consent to it, so a teen cannot have their account limited against their will. Theoretically, anyway. A parent account can supervise as many as five teen accounts, but a teen account can only be linked to one parent account.

This is interesting because it's an acknowledgment by X that some teenagers do use the platform, but even in the Safety account's post, the company is clear that X is "not designed for or promoted to children." Indeed, one could argue that teen owners should stay far away from a service that has become home to hate speech, widespread misinformation, and a Grok AI chatbot that has gotten up to plenty of unsavory business since it was introduced.

But if teens are going to use X, at least these features exist now.

Sources indicate that recently, UGREEN introduced a fresh Qi2.2 25W 10000mAh MagSafe battery bank for iPhone. There have been plenty of these, but this one has an interesting new twist: liquid cooling. For Black Friday, it’s on sale for 40% off, making it more affordable than ever.

In a recent development, on the back of the battery, there’s a window that showcases the liquid within the battery bank moving throughout it. This should help keep it a little bit cooler than most MagSafe battery banks.

UGREEN states that it’ll be around 18 degrees cooler than usual, and while that’s probably true – it’s worth nothing that it still isn’t a cold battery bank, it’s just cooler than usual. It’ll still feel warm in your hand.

Sources indicate that on the bottom of the battery bank, UGREEN integrates a USB-C cable for charging your phone or any other USB-C device that can’t (or you prefer not to) charge wirelessly. I found it a bit handy at times, since of course wireless charging is never as energy efficient as wired charging.

In a recent development, I will admit, the battery bank is a little bit thick, and the lack of a kickstand is somewhat bothersome at this price point, especially when so many others offer one. That noted, if heat is a concern of yours with MagSafe battery banks, this one will definitely solve that for you.

On the side, it offers a small display for showing battery percentage and charging speed.

One last thing of note: if you’re buying an iPhone Duo, this will stick out from the bottom of the phone. This is true for most MagSafe accessories on iPhone Duo, though.

According to recent reports, the UGREEN MagFlow battery bank comes in at $149, which is quite pricey for a MagSafe battery of any kind. For Black Friday, it’s on sale for just $90.23 on Amazon for Prime members, making it much more palatable if you’re looking for a MagSafe battery bank that doesn’t get as hot as the competition.

  • Recent findings suggest that while he notes that this cycle runs between February and March, it doesn’t necessarily mean the products will launch on the earlier end of that spectrum.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of Apple’s most beloved products this year was undoubtedly the MacBook Neo. Unlike some of its other budget products, Apple seems interested in updating the MacBook Neo on an annual cycle, and we may get the next MacBook Neo around March.

According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple is targeting the iOS/macOS 27.4 release cycle for the release of the latest MacBook Neo, as well as the A19 budget iPad, iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and OLED iPad Air.

Recent findings suggest that while he notes that this cycle runs between February and March, it doesn’t necessarily mean the products will launch on the earlier end of that spectrum. Apple is also expected to release the iPhone Air 2, OLED iPad Air, and a latest iPad Pro within the first half of the year, but they’ll likely come a bit later than the aforementioned products.

As expected, the next MacBook Neo will bump up from the A18 Pro chip with 8GB of RAM to the A19 Pro chip with 12GB of RAM.

Industry observers note that apple will also introduce new colors on the MacBook Neo “frequently,” though it’s unclear if we’ll see that with the next iteration. From the Power On newsletter:.

It has been revealed that the other thing I’ve heard is that Apple looks to refresh the MacBook Neo’s colors frequently. We’ll see if that trend starts with the first follow-up.

I’m certainly excited to see the next generation MacBook Neo, especially with 12GB of unified memory. While 8GB is certainly fine, heavy multitaskers will notice it, especially with unoptimized software.

Industry observers note that the bigger question is: will the next MacBook Neo have a price increase? With additional RAM included, it feels inevitable.

Hopefully backlit keyboard if they increase price.

Apple increased the price of MacBook Neo from $599 to $699 back in June, and in October the tech giant also silently decreased the education discount by $50, meaning the education price has increased from $499 to $649 since launch.

If there is a price increase, it likely won’t be too major, maybe $50 – leaving the computer at $749. Compared to the rest of the laptop landscape, MacBook Neo would still be a good value. We’ll see what happens.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Upgrade: It turns out that this feature is actually referenced in the User Guide for iPhone Duo.

Industry observers note that apple made a bunch of changes to iOS to optimize it for the iPhone Duo’s form factor, including revamping the Lock Screen. According to a fresh leak today, the company has tested another change, referred to as a “complication column.” Here’s what it looks like.

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

Industry observers note that on the iPhone Duo’s Lock Screen right now, you can add widgets along the bottom of the interface. On the bottom right, you have two controls that default to the flashlight and camera. You can customize these and link them to other controls from Apple and third-party apps.

Cellular and Wi-Fi information is located along the top right-hand side of the iPhone Duo’s Lock Screen.

According to the spelunking account pdfu on X, Apple has tested a “complication column” that would appear along the right edge of the Lock Screen. The column has room for two widgets, filling the space between the flashlight/camera controls and the Wi-Fi and cellular status icons. These widgets are the same size as the widgets that appear along the bottom.

The “complication column” for iPhone Duo was first spotted in iOS 27.1 code, the account says. No code changes have been made since, so it’s unclear whether the feature is still in active development or Apple has scrapped it.

Apple has tested a “complication column” for iPhone Duo’s Lock Screen. It fits two circular widgets along the right edge.Flag: SpringBoard/Ionic (disabled). First seen in iOS 27.1, with no code changes since. pic.twitter.com/orjOuvM1Xs.

I think this looks great. It’s fun seeing Apple try different things as it learns how to best design for the iPhone Duo’s form factor, which is so different from a traditional iPhone. I’d be especially intrigued to try this on the inner display’s Lock Screen, where there’s currently a lot of wasted space.

According to recent reports, I hope this “complication column” idea is still in development and makes it into a future iOS 27 revision. What about you? Let us know down in the comments.

iOS 27 includes a really clever fresh feature that aims to solve the awkward middle ground between cellular and Wi-Fi connectivity. Here’s how it works and how you can turn it on.

Industry observers note that in a support document, Apple explains that Connectivity Assist uses cellular data to improve your connection when Wi-Fi is slow or unusable. Apple uses examples like your backyard or driveway, as well as “coffee shops, airports, sports venues, and everywhere in between.”.

Essentially, the feature detects when your Wi-Fi connection is weak or unusable and intelligently uses cellular data to keep you connected.

One practical example I’ve noticed is when I walk out of my house and get in my car. Oftentimes, my iPhone will cling to my house’s weak Wi-Fi connection, making it hard to start playing Apple Music and queue up directions in Apple Maps.

It has been revealed that connectivity Assist solves that problem. My phone can now intelligently use cellular data to help that transition away from Wi-Fi. It’s one of many really nice quality-of-life improvements in iOS 27.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, everyone's journey through Grand Theft Auto VI is going to go a little differently, as that's the nature of a big, freeform open-world adventure. But one thing is certain for every player: You're going to need money, and fast.

It has been revealed that that's especially true at the beginning of chapter 2 of the game's main story. For reasons I won't spoil in case you aren't there yet, chapter 2 finds Jason and Lucia in a tough spot with almost no money to their names, and an urgent need to get some. Thankfully, there are a couple of different methods that, when combined, can net you somewhere between $15,000 and $20,000, with almost no killing or even any real effort required.

Just understand that there may be some minor spoilers for the beginning of chapter 2 if you decide to read ahead.

We'll start with a method to get at least $10,000 (and possibly as much as $14,000), which we first learned about from GamingBible and tested ourselves to ensure it worked. Without beating around the bush, it does work.

It involves going to an abandoned warehouse outside the town of Hamlet, which is easily accessible from the very beginning of the game. However, because (spoiler warning) you lose all of your held money at the end of chapter 1, I highly advise waiting until chapter 2 to do this.

Sources indicate that anyway, you'll know you're in the right place if you follow the waypoint marker in the screenshot above and see a warehouse with an Apollo sign out front. There will be lots of vehicles and construction equipment outside, but don't worry, it's totally empty inside. Well, except for a bunch of rotting corpses and more than $10,000 worth of contraband lying around. Simply pick all of it up, stash it in the trunk of your car, and take it to a fence for a low-effort, no-risk payday. Just make sure you have a fence available to you when you do this. You'll unlock one early in chapter 2, so perhaps you should work your way through a few main story missions at the beginning of the chapter before taking this on. It's also logistically a little easier to do this with both Jason and Lucia together, as there is a lot to carry in there, so maybe keep playing until that's an option, too.

It has been revealed that this second batch of cash is one we heard about from our friends at IGN, and, again, we can vouch for it ourselves. It's something you can only do after the start of chapter 2, but just to reiterate, you are pretty destitute with almost no money and no vehicles to your name at that point in the game. It's worth playing a couple of story missions to at least fix the vehicle problem first before doing this next bit of money-stealing.

To be specific, there is a "rainy day fund" of $5,000 cash hidden in Jason's bedroom in his old house. Unfortunately, by this point in the game, that house has been exploded real good, and the entire neighborhood is a heat area where cops are stationed and looking for Jason and Lucia. It's a bit of a hike from where the story takes place in chapter 2, and it's in a risky spot, so this is a super easy wad of cash to miss.

Sources indicate that still, you can at least drive (or take a cab) down to the area outside the heat zone and go on foot from there. Do whatever you can to sneak to the backside of Jason's house and get inside. You can easily evade the cops if you stick to nearby backyards and maybe do a little bit of swimming. Just stay crouched and quiet, and you'll get in and out easily. Once you're in, go to Jason's old bedroom, open the stash, and grab the $5,000. You can also optionally grab some old photos while you're at it, which will raise Jason and Lucia's relationship rating.

In a recent development, if you do both of these things, which should take maybe half an hour of real-time at most, you can roll around in chapter 2 with as much as $19,000 in your account before you get started doing real crimes. Have fun, folks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AirPods Pro 3 (now only $149, down from $249) offer many advantages over AirPods Pro 2, but after a year of use, the improvements to Active Noise Cancellation alone have proven worth the upgrade.

Sources indicate that I’ve been using AirPods Pro 3 for over a year, and they had a lot to live up to because I already loved AirPods Pro 2 so much. Initially I found the newly introduced ear tips less comfortable, but thankfully that matter went away after a little extra time.

Some highlights of AirPods Pro 3 include the longer battery life, with 8 hours per charge compared to 6 on the previous model. The charging case’s new Ultra Wideband chip also makes it easier to find when it’s lost. Some consumers will appreciate the heart rate sensor, but I wear an Apple Watch all the time so it doesn’t benefit me much.

Sources indicate that these upcoming features are nice to have, but Active Noise Cancellation is where AirPods Pro 3 become a major upgrade. Apple says it’s “the world’s best in-ear Active Noise Cancellation.” Here’s how the new ANC compares to previous models:.

Sources indicate that I spend nearly my entire workday with AirPods Pro 3 in my ears. Whether I’m working from home with young kids around or at a busy coffee shop, I rely on ANC to block out background noise and help me focus.

Sources indicate that one reason I’ve been especially impressed with the ANC upgrades is that I didn’t have any real complaints about ANC on AirPods Pro 2. But Apple managed to deliver improvements in AirPods Pro 3 I had no idea I needed, and when I’ve tried going back to AirPods Pro 2 I couldn’t believe how much noise was let in.

If Active Noise Cancellation is key to you, I highly recommend AirPods Pro 3.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27.3 is coming soon, and it’s a significant revision for upcoming iPhone features, including additions that span six built-in Apple apps. Here’s what’s new.

Apple Music adds a pair of upgrades in iOS 27.3. Selfie Sing is an all-new feature that lets you record short videos of yourself singing along to your favorite songs, aided by onscreen lyrics. It’s perfect for sharing on TikTok or other social platforms.

If you’re not the type to share karaoke videos online, another nice iOS 27.3 change is that the lyrics view for songs has gotten an iPhone Duo-inspired upgrade in landscape mode. Now, artwork for the song you’re listening to blends beautifully into the stream of lyrics.

Read more: iOS 27.3 upgrades Apple Music in two ways, here’s what’s new.

Safari is getting several exciting newly introduced features in iOS 27.3, including:.

Read more: iOS 27.3 and macOS 27.3 add Vertical Tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode, and more to Safari.

Apple’s Health app gets a major overhaul in iOS 27.3, though only for Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhones.

The new Health app has an Insights tab for personalized data visualization and guidance, Longevity tab for tracking your health age, and there are new features like educational videos, movement evaluations, and the ability to order labs that get automatically imported into the app.

Read more: iOS 27.3 adds all-latest Apple Health app, details here.

Vertical video is coming with a fresh Clips feature that lets you browse short samples of Apple TV shows and movies in a TikTok-style vertically scrolling format.

Video podcasts are also coming to the TV app, with the option to automatically sync playback from Apple Podcasts inside the TV app.

Read more: iOS 27.3 brings vertical video and video podcasts to Apple TV app.

Apple Fitness+ is getting a massive expansion in iOS 27.3 with a new Gym Strength program.

Gym Strength lets you build a strength program that fits your schedule and the equipment you have on hand. It’s fully customizable and provides Apple’s best offering yet for traditional strength training.

Whether you’re brand new to strength training or just benefit from some additional structure, Gym Strength is a great reason to try out Fitness+.

Read more: Apple reveals Fitness+ Gym Strength program with personalized workout looks.

Industry observers note that apple’s Freeform app gets a handful of improvements in iOS 27.3, including newly introduced text styling options and preset background colors to choose from. You can also generate custom shapes using Apple Intelligence.

Which fresh iOS 27.3 features are you most excited about? Let us know in the comments.

Apple TV is available for just $6.99/ month (over 50% off) for a limited time, with the offer ending Monday, November 30.

Recent findings suggest that kick-starting your fresh year's fitness goals is better stated than done, but believe me, once you have a good smartwatch or fitness tracker cuffed to your wrist, it helps you build a better understanding of your health patterns, helping you build a better relationship with your body. Industry observers note that ✅Recommended if: Your current Fitbit doesn't pack Google's slew of health tracking tools, and you want the upgrade. Due to its small bezel, it's a wonder to wear while you sleep, which I've found frustrating with wearables — particularly smartwatches.

According to recent reports, if you prefer smaller wearables that aren't too obtrusive, but still pack the punch with smarts, the Fitbit Charge 6 does just that. With three GPS settings, AFib detection, heart rate variability, breathing rate, and blood oxygen tracking, its small build packs quite the roster of features.

According to recent reports, ❌Skip this deal if: You want a fitness tracker with a larger, brighter screen. The Fitbit Charge 6 has all the smarts you need for a wearable, but in comparison to other models, its screen isn't the easiest to navigate. The Fitbit Charge 6 works to its full potential with a Google Health Premium subscription too, which is another setback if you don't want to pay for more than the device itself.

Recent findings suggest that however, the only features you'll miss out on if you go subscription-free are Daily Readiness and guided workout programs, which not everyone needs. Other than that, it does pretty much everything else you need, so a subscription isn't a big requirement.

So imagine my shock when I checked Amazon's MacBook Air listings first thing Thanksgiving morning and spotted several 13-inch models on sale for at least $300 off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Nest app is officially dead, but it’s worth taking a step back and remembering that, while there are some rough edges, the Google Home app is a better smart home experience than Nest alone ever could have been.

In a recent development, the Nest app has been on life support for years now. Google has been migrating legacy products into the Home app for a while and the last few puzzle pieces came in Nest Protect support, the death of the earliest Nest Thermostats, and other assorted adjustments.

Realistically, even long-time Nest users have had no reason to continue using the app over Google Home.

It has been revealed that having been personally, deeply invested in Google’s vision for the smart home over the past decade, I’ll say that the Google Home app we have today is better than the Nest app ever was or ever could be. A huge part of that comes from Google Home’s ability to pull together devices from third-party ecosystems. Being able to control your entire smart home from a single app is how the smart home always should have been, and between Google’s work and the Matter standard, we’re finally able to enjoy that pretty seamlessly for the most part. Automations, Google’s actually-useful AI features, and more only sweeten the deal. I’m also a major fan of what the Home app has become from a UX perspective. While there are always rough edges and bugs to clean up, the customizable homepage and well-organized sections make for a good – not perfect, but good – experience for the end user.

That said, there is one thing that the Nest app’s limited scope benefitted from, and that’s a focus on making your own product great.

Industry observers note that google’s move to the Home app for Nest devices has been a 5-year run of trying to clean things up, improve on the app, and basically bring back the way things were in the Nest app as far as the first-party cameras and thermostats are concerned. It’s taken ages, but we’re finally up to speed, mostly. I still hate that you have to reset Nest Cams to change Wi-Fi when the Nest app just let you change it, and the Nest app’s settings were much less overwhelming, but I’d say the pros far outweigh the cons at this point.

It has been revealed that the Nest app was good at its job, but the Google Home app is a worthy successor, finally, and now the Nest app can finally rest. I mostly think the same applies to Gemini vs Google Assistant, with the newer assistant a better overall experience, but it’s easier to poke holes in that argument.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Workers voted 75 percent against the IWGB recognition agreement.

Workers voted 75 percent against the IWGB recognition agreement.

Workers at Grand Theft Auto VI developer Rockstar Games won’t unionize, after the vote for a formal recognition agreement failed, with only 25 percent of votes in favor of unionization. The Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB) stated that Rockstar workers in the union will continue organizing even without formal recognition.

In a recent development, voting ran from November 12th through 26th, covering the launch of GTA VI. If successful, the vote would have established a formal framework for collective negotiation with the studio over pay, overtime, bonuses, leave, and pensions, along with a right to consultation over future changes including AI implementation and layoffs. Without it, Rockstar won’t have an obligation to meet union representatives, though workers and union members can still lobby for change informally.

“For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society - this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for,” IWGB said in a statement sent to The Verge. “Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.”.

When Rockstar fired 31 IWGB members last year, the union accused it of “the most blatant and ruthless act of union busting in the history of the games industry.” That case has gone to a UK employment tribunal, with a judgment still pending.

“We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we’ve built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI,” Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe told Bloomberg News. “This result reflects our team’s strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we’re excited to build on all we’ve accomplished together.”.

Both also get five years of Wear OS updates and security patches, making either a useful long-term partner for your Samsung device, like the Galaxy S26 Ultra or Galaxy Z Fold8.

It has been revealed that the clearest differences are size, battery capacity, display brightness, and outdoor capabilities. Here’s how the lineup breaks down:.

As you can tell, the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is considerably bigger and heavier, but you get a lot more capability for that additional size.

The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 makes its strongest case when your plans regularly take you beyond a desk, a gym, or a charger.

Samsung rates the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 for up to 60 hours with the always-on display enabled, compared with up to 30 hours for the Watch 9, and that extra headroom is appealing when your day starts with a workout and finishes well into the evening.

Then there’s the screen. In our hands-on with both watches, the Ultra 2’s brightness stood out immediately, with a higher peak that gives it an advantage when checking workout information outdoors, even in the bright sun. And its titanium frame provides added durability.

Sources indicate that the Ultra 2 also adds Trail Run tracking for elevation and terrain impact, route guidance using compatible GPX files, and Nutrition Alert hydration guidance. These are tangible reasons to upgrade if your usual run involves trails instead of pavement.

Diving is another differentiator. Samsung specifies recreational diving support to depths of up to 40 meters, with automatic tracking of depth, dive time and water temperature — a remarkable feat for a piece of technology that lives on your wrist.

The best choice becomes clearer when you picture your own routine:.

Choose the Galaxy Watch 9 for everyday wellness, a lighter fit, and strong value. Choose the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 for longer adventures, more demanding outdoor activities, and greater freedom between charges.

Sources indicate that if you’re replacing an older Galaxy Watch, both offer a compelling latest generation of health insights and long-term support. Both last a long time and look absolutely awesome with running shorts or a business suit. But the Watch Ultra 2 can take you that extra mile, literally and figuratively, and may be worth spending more on during Best Buy’s Holiday Deals event.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google this weekend rolled out the latest update to Pixel Weather with a newly introduced reporting feature and small interface tweaks.

Sources indicate that on the homepage, cities that have active weather warnings no longer have bright red card backgrounds. The pill-shaped container retains its Dynamic Color theming with just the text of the warning in red. This change also extends to the card on the city page. Finally, the source, like “Google Weather,” at the very bottom is now themed.

The main change today is a “Report current weather” feature to “Share the current weather condition to improve local forecasts.” The card appears at the very bottom of your current location and can be moved up the feed.

Google claims to “Submit a report if the weather conditions don’t look right.” Tapping “Submit a report” brings up a “Report weather in [city]” sheet. You can submit two pieces of information:.

According to recent reports, on the privacy front: “Your feedback, device location and some diagnostic information will be collected to help improve forecasts. This information will not be associated with your Google account.”.

This is rolling out with version 1.1.20261012.x of Pixel Weather that widely rolled out this weekend.

#3232. MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air: Which should you buy right now?

MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air: Which should you buy right now?

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (768 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple’s Mac lineup is stronger than ever this year, largely thanks to the newly introduced MacBook Neo.
  • The MacBook Neo is Apple’s most affordable laptop ever, starting at $699 (currently on sale for $599).
  • Unlike Apple’s other Macs, the MacBook Neo is powered by an A-series chip rather than an M-series chip.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s Mac lineup is stronger than ever this year, largely thanks to the newly introduced MacBook Neo. If you’re deciding between the MacBook Neo and the MacBook Air this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

The MacBook Neo is Apple’s most affordable laptop ever, starting at $699 (currently on sale for $599). It features a solid aluminum design that comes in a range of fun colors, including Silver, Blush, Citrus, and Indigo.

Unlike Apple’s other Macs, the MacBook Neo is powered by an A-series chip rather than an M-series chip. It uses the A18 Pro chip originally introduced with the iPhone 16 Pro, featuring a 6-core CPU and 5-core GPU.

The MacBook Neo comes with 8GB of unified memory, with no additional RAM configuration options available. It starts with 256GB of storage, with a 512GB configuration available for an additional $100. That $100 upgrade also gets you Touch ID, which is not included in the base model.

There are some other trade-offs compared to the MacBook Air. The MacBook Neo lacks a backlit keyboard, MagSafe charging, and a Force Touch trackpad. It also has more limited USB-C connectivity and supports just one external display.

In a recent development, still, the MacBook Neo offers an impressive feature set. It has a 13-inch display, up to 16 hours of battery life, a 1080p FaceTime camera, and the full macOS experience.

It has been revealed that the MacBook Air, meanwhile, was updated earlier this year with Apple’s M5 chip. It starts at $1,299, making it $600 more expensive than the entry-level MacBook Air. The MacBook Air is currently on sale with a starting price of $999.

For that $600 upgrade, the MacBook Air offers several key advantages over the MacBook Air. The M5 chip has a 10-core CPU and up to a 10-core GPU, enabling better sustained performance than the MacBook Neo.

The MacBook Air also starts with 16GB of unified memory and 512GB of storage, both double the entry-level MacBook Neo. You can configure it with up to 32GB of memory and 4TB of storage, while the MacBook Neo is limited to 8GB of memory and 512GB of storage.

Apple rates the MacBook Air for up to 18 hours of video streaming and 15 hours of wireless web browsing, compared to 16 hours and 11 hours, respectively, for the MacBook Neo.

As I wrote in my review earlier this year, I think the MacBook Neo is a great Mac, full stop … not just because of the great price. It can handle the vast majority of things most people will throw at it. This includes web browsing, basic photo and video editing, research, and much more.

The M5 MacBook Air, meanwhile, offers more power and more configuration options. This makes it a great option for people who need more storage, RAM, and power than the MacBook Neo can offer.

According to recent reports, one of my favorite things about the MacBook Air is that it’s available in two screen sizes. The 15-inch MacBook Air is one of my favorite Apple laptops with a combination of the ultra-thin and light design and the larger screen. I think a lot of people forget it exists, but it’s an excellent choice.

To recap, I think the MacBook Neo is a great choice for everyday tasks like web browsing, email, writing, and streaming. The MacBook Air is a better fit for more demanding workflows, including photo and video editing, coding, working with large spreadsheets, and heavy multitasking.

Beyond performance, the MacBook Air offers a handful of niceties that you won’t find on the MacBook Neo. These include a backlit keyboard, a larger display with True Tone, MagSafe charging, a better webcam and speakers, and a Force Touch trackpad. It also includes Touch ID on every configuration, longer battery life, and support for two external displays.

If it’s in the budget, I think the MacBook Air is an excellent choice for all Mac shoppers. It’s plenty powerful, thin and light, and is highly configurable compared to the MacBook Neo.

What do you think of the MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air decision? Which would you choose? Let us know down in the comments.

Industry News: Federal judge blocks the FCC from reviewing ABC’s licenses early

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (325 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: The Verge

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The judge has preliminarily sided with ABC, rejecting the FCC’s efforts to dismiss the case.﻿.
  • The judge has preliminarily sided with ABC, rejecting the FCC’s efforts to dismiss the case.﻿.
  • Sources indicate that US District Judge Loren AliKhan has blocked the Federal Communications Commission from conducting an early review of ABC’s broadcast licenses in a preliminary injunction, and rejected its efforts to dismiss ABC’s First Amendment lawsuit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The judge has preliminarily sided with ABC, rejecting the FCC’s efforts to dismiss the case.﻿.

The judge has preliminarily sided with ABC, rejecting the FCC’s efforts to dismiss the case.﻿.

Sources indicate that US District Judge Loren AliKhan has blocked the Federal Communications Commission from conducting an early review of ABC’s broadcast licenses in a preliminary injunction, and rejected its efforts to dismiss ABC’s First Amendment lawsuit. ABC has accused the FCC of violating its free speech rights and claims the agency “waged a retaliatory campaign” against the network over content it broadcast. In her ruling the judge noted that the network was “likely to succeed on their retaliation claim.”.

According to recent reports, although Disney, ABC’s parent organization, wasn’t set to renew its broadcast licenses until 2028, last April the FCC ordered the network to file for an early license renewal claiming it was part of an investigation into Disney’s policies on diversity, equity, and inclusivity. The FCC’s move came a day after President Donald Trump demanded ABC fire late-night talk show host Jimmy Kimmel following a skit about Melania Trump.

Recent findings suggest that in response to the FCC’s order, Disney and ABC sued the agency in August and accused the FCC of “punishing ABC for its speech” by threatening its broadcast licenses. The preliminary injunction issued by the judge on Wednesday prohibits the FCC from taking any further action in the early review of ABC’s broadcast licenses and noted that the network had shown that the court’s intervention in the agency’s actions was in the public interest.

Recent findings suggest that ”No one doubts that the Commission may enforce the law in the manner it sees fit,” the judge wrote. “But in doing so, Defendants may not retaliate against or punish Plaintiffs and other broadcast license holders for disfavored speech.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When I'm in a rush to leave the house, there's only one pair of earbuds that I shove into my pocket without a second thought: the Beats Solo Buds.

They're extremely compact and lightweight thanks to a sophisticated design that ditches the usual clunky earpod case battery and instead crams 18 hours of juice into each bud on a single charge, so they're easy to take on the go.

Industry observers note that better still, their Fast Fuel quick-charging feature means that you can squeeze an hour of playback out of a single hour of charge – and this is something I rely on all the time. I plug the buds directly into my phone's charging port when they're dead for a quick charge when I need a bit of extra juice. It's a real lifesaver and means that, as long as I carry a small cable, I never have to worry about being without my tunes.

Sources indicate that at just £39 (was £79), thanks to a mega EE discount, they're also simply incredible value and pack in plenty of that trademark Beats sound despite the small form factor. Beats may be owned by Apple, but that doesn't mean the Solo Buds don't play nice with Android. They support Google Fast Pair, and even have an Android companion app. (If you are an Apple user, they work perfectly with that ecosystem, too.).

These compact earbuds are a steal at under £40. They come in a wide range of attractive colors (though the translucent red is my personal favorite) and are both practical and stylish. EE is even throwing in free delivery.

✅Recommended if: You're after a seriously compact pair of earbuds that you won't need to worry about keeping charged.

According to recent reports, the Beats Solo Buds are some of the smallest and lightest wireless earbuds I've ever used when in their case, making them easy to take on the go. The Fast Fuel feature also makes them very quick to top up with charge, even when you're out and about.

Recent findings suggest that ❌Skip this deal if: You want to spend more and get better sound. Although I think the Beats Solo Buds can hold their own in the under £100 audio space with their poppy and bassy sound, the brand doesn't exactly have a reputation for audiophile quality.

If you want to spend more on something that sounds even better, you have plenty of options to choose from in the ongoing sales.

Sources indicate that TL;DR: Scramble Cloud’s 20TB lifetime subscription is down to $314.96 (reg. $1,440) this Black Friday with code CLOUD, offering encrypted cloud storage without recurring fees.

It has been revealed that nobody needs 87 nearly identical photos of their dog, but who has the heart to delete them? If you’re the sentimental type when it comes to your digital files, Scramble Cloud is offering 20TB of lifetime cloud storage for $314.96 (reg. $1,440) this Black Friday with the code CLOUD.

That’s plenty of room for years of family photos, vacation videos, work documents, and those random files you’re convinced will come in handy someday. And with that much personal data sitting in one place, privacy is worth considering.

Developed in Germany, Scramble Cloud uses end-to-end encryption to protect files before they even leave your device, along with a zero-knowledge architecture designed to prevent the provider from accessing your stored content. Two-factor authentication adds another layer of account protection.

Scramble Cloud isn’t just a digital dumping ground, either. You can organize documents using a familiar folder structure, preview compatible files in your browser, and stream MP4 videos directly from your account. And if you’d like to subject your family to all those vacation photos, private sharing links, encrypted groups, and customizable file permissions let you decide who gets access to what. 📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • The change is to meet EU regulations, but Apple gives its developers more privacy.﻿.
  • Independent Android app developers are worried about their privacy after Google revealed that from next year many of them will be required to share a phone number and address publicly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The change is to meet EU regulations, but Apple gives its developers more privacy.﻿.

The change is to meet EU regulations, but Apple gives its developers more privacy.﻿.

Independent Android app developers are worried about their privacy after Google revealed that from next year many of them will be required to share a phone number and address publicly. The policy change is intended to meet European Union regulations under the Digital Services Act, but Google says contact details will be made public worldwide.

Developers have until February 1st 2027 to declare whether or not they’re a “trader” under UK and European law. Broadly speaking, Google indicates the definition applies if you earn revenue from your apps, especially if that revenue is regular or at high volume. Developers are exempt if their apps are only a hobby or non-commercial, or if they simply don’t publish them in the UK or Europe.

Industry observers note that if they self-declare as a trader, developers’ contact details will be shared publicly starting March 1st, including a phone number and address. Google doesn’t accept PO boxes for developer payment profile addresses, meaning many independent developers without an office will either have to share their home address online or pay for a registered agent or other service that provides a business address. One independent developer told The Elec they were considering renting a private office solely to comply with the new rules. We’ve asked Google to confirm why developers aren’t permitted to publish a PO box address, and why details are being shared globally, and will revision this article when we hear back.

Sources indicate that apple is subject to the same regulations, but is handling them differently to Google. It will only display developer addresses within the relevant European countries, rather than publishing them worldwide. It’s also allowing developers to supply PO box addresses, so long as they provide Apple with a receipt or bill that links the PO box to their regular address.

Update, November 26th: Added mention of developers’ option to use a registered agent service for a business address.

#3219. Breaking: Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn’t a virtue

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1320 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn’t a virtue

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1320 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it should have been impossible for “Grand Theft Auto VI” (GTA VI) to live up to the hype.
  • GTA VI debuted as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and made $3.79 billion on release day to mark what could be the biggest entertainment event ever – more massive than “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.9 billion) or Taylor Swift’s Eras tour ($2 billion).
  • The 13-year wait certainly fueled the frenzy, and sales, around GTA VI, but some fans craved GTA VI because of what it represents in the emerging era of AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it should have been impossible for “Grand Theft Auto VI” (GTA VI) to live up to the hype. Fans waited 13 years for the newest installment in the crime-adventure franchise, and Rockstar Games exceeded even those inconceivable expectations when the game finally came out last week.

GTA VI debuted as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and made $3.79 billion on release day to mark what could be the biggest entertainment event ever – more massive than “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.9 billion) or Taylor Swift’s Eras tour ($2 billion).

The 13-year wait certainly fueled the frenzy, and sales, around GTA VI, but some fans craved GTA VI because of what it represents in the emerging era of AI.

Even the biggest workaholics among us – startup founders – scheduled time off to play the game, including Spiry co-founder Dima Beseda, who told TechCrunch, “I reshuffled my workload to free up time around the weekends and even booked vitamin IV drips to keep my energy up.”.

Yet some players felt a sense of anticipatory nostalgia as they wiped away a layer of dust on their Xbox to play the game they’d been looking forward to since they were kids.

“We do have a view that GTA is likely to be the last game of its kind to be made this way,” Ben Feder, managing partner at TIRTA Ventures and former CEO of Rockstar parent manufacturer Take-Two Interactive, told TechCrunch.

That’s because GTA VI was created entirely without generative AI.

“We’re kind of at this technological moment where this way of developing has sort of reached its natural frontier,” Feder remarked. “I don’t think you can say that games like this will always be around.”.

As millions of people immersed themselves in Vice City, the tech industry witnessed another long-awaited moment: Anthropic became the first major AI lab to go public. At Nasdaq HQ, Anthropic executives gathered to celebrate the Claude maker’s $81.3 billion IPO. At virtually the same moment that Anthropic broke the record for the largest IPO ever, GTA VI was also breaking records with the highest-rated and best-selling game launch of all time.

But when the Anthropic team rang the bell on Thursday, the sound also signaled the end of an era in video game development, and perhaps even in the arts at large.

The AI industry operates with efficiency as its north star. The promise of this technology is that we will be able to automate so much work that we can expand the capabilities of humanity, avoiding needless time spent tinkering with ultimately fruitless ideas. Instead, a prompt goes into an LLM, and a response is spat out.

This technological revolution exploded into the world with some soul-crushing side effects: children are inundated with mind-numbing slop on YouTube, lawyers cite nonexistent cases in court, and tech companies like Meta lay off tens of thousands of people as part of a corporate-branded “Year of Efficiency.” But against the backdrop of the AI industry’s first major IPO, Rockstar has unveiled a game that about 5,000 people labored over for more than a decade.

Industry observers note that the final product is breathtaking, looking so lifelike that it can be hard to distinguish gameplay footage from real life. These sprawling open-world games are usually made possible by procedurally generating latest landscapes and objects, but Rockstar has taken the time to painstakingly craft every detail of the world, even developing 30,000 different nonplayable characters with unique appearances and personalities.

Sources indicate that the video game industry is already grappling with the threat of AI. Google’s Project Genie, which launched earlier this year, allows users to create and wander around 3D worlds generated from prompts to an LLM. The stock prices of several video game companies faltered around the time of Project Genie’s release, perhaps because of investors’ uncertainty about the future relevance of video game developers.

Sources indicate that “The notion that somehow newly introduced tools would allow an individual to push a button and generate a hit, market a hit, and bring it to many millions of consumers around the world, it’s a laughable notion,” Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick said at the time. “It’s just never been the case with entertainment.”.

Recent findings suggest that zelnick’s fellow tech CEOs see different future, though. On a Meta earnings call this year, CEO Mark Zuckerberg promised that, “soon, you’ll have an AI that understands you and [can] even generate great personalized content for you.”.

Elon Musk even went as far as proposing that a game like GTA VI could be made with AI.

Recent findings suggest that “You won’t even have to ask,” Musk wrote on X. “AI will figure what video game you’d like best.”.

This is the paradox of “Grandthropic” week. GTA VI is so impressively vast and captivating because its developers could make mistakes, experiment, and rework ideas, even if that meant delaying the game (twice). GTA VI was incubated with the exact inefficiencies that investors hope AI companies like Anthropic can help eradicate.

“Plenty of fantastic art — video games and elsewhere — almost by definition has to be created slowly, and there’s something to having that kind of inefficiency around it,” Feder stated. “Creative output requires deletion, right? Getting to kind of a masterpiece oftentimes requires an enormous amount of deletion. And when you’re talking about a game of the kind of complexity we’re talking about, that kind of deletion ends up being very expensive, and it is by definition not efficient.”.

GTA VI reeks of its own humanity – every small detail is loaded with intention, but it’s this impressive precision that keeps the world abuzz, triggering the kind of monocultural moment that has become increasingly rare in a media landscape that revolves around highly personalized social media algorithms.

The game forces the player to slow down, which is either frustrating or genius, depending on your sense of humor. People waited more than three presidential terms for the next installment in a high-octane action franchise, only to download a 212 GB behemoth of a game in which your earliest missions involve driving around doing errands and putting up drywall to make your girlfriend happy. Don’t worry — there are still car chases and shootouts — but in a moment when AI feels suffocating, GTA VI is such an artistic achievement that it is reaching audiences that don’t even like violent video games.

The ultimate fantasy of GTA VI is no longer to role-play as a criminal — the fantasy is just taking your time to relish the mundane and explore an expansive world that developers were given the time and space to perfect.

#3218. Judge orders Apple to produce 3,200 documents in Epic Games dispute

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (905 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5mac ↗ Open Full Page

Judge orders Apple to produce 3,200 documents in Epic Games dispute

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (905 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A federal judge has ordered Apple to produce a random sample of 3,200 documents for Epic Games to review, following Epic’s allegations that Apple improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions.
  • With Apple and Epic trading arguments in the Supreme Court over whether the civil contempt ruling against Apple should stand, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.
  • In August, Apple submitted its proposal to the district court, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A federal judge has ordered Apple to produce a random sample of 3,200 documents for Epic Games to review, following Epic’s allegations that Apple improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions. Here are the details.

With Apple and Epic trading arguments in the Supreme Court over whether the civil contempt ruling against Apple should stand, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

In August, Apple submitted its proposal to the district court, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%. Epic, however, is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.

Earlier this month, Epic accused Apple of improperly withholding more than 122,000 documents matching a set of search terms agreed upon by both companies to help identify documents that could shed light on how Apple arrived at those rates.

[…] Apple is withholding well over 99% of the documents returned by running the agreed-to search terms on the files of the four custodians Apple says decided on the proposed fee (Tim Cook, Eddy Cue, Carson Oliver, and Kevan Parekh (Apple’s latest CFO)) and three other key individuals (Nate Barton, Alex Roman, and Phil Schiller). Apple claims these withheld documents are not relevant to this proceeding-even though they hit on case-specific terms such as “proffer,” “contempt,” “injunction,” and “link-out.” To put this into context, while Apple produced 632 custodial documents returned by these search terms (including families), Apple is withholding over 122,000 based on a claim of non-responsiveness.

Apple, in turn, pushed back against Epic’s accusations, saying the search terms were overly broad and had captured large numbers of documents unrelated to the proceedings.

[…] at least 95% of the Initial Custodian Document Population hit on generic terms […]. These sweeping terms do not just increase the total volume of the Initial Custodian Document Population, they also captured highly sensitive and irrelevant documents, such as Apple employees’ personal tax or financial records, medical records, documents discussing unannounced products, documents containing passwords, investor-relations materials, and privileged or protected legal communications.

The organization also asked the court to reject Epic’s motion to order it to produce all non-privileged documents matching the agreed-upon search terms, and alternatively suggested submitting a randomized, statistically significant sample of the documents it deemed nonresponsive to a Special Master for independent review.

As it turns out, neither manufacturer got exactly what it originally wanted, but the judge ruled largely in Epic’s favor on how to determine whether Apple had improperly withheld documents.

Recent findings suggest that following a hearing in which both companies presented their respective proposals for how a randomized sampling of the documents should be conducted, Magistrate Judge Thomas S. Hixson decided to adopt Epic’s proposal, which called for Apple to produce a random sample of 3,200 documents it had previously deemed nonresponsive, along with their associated document families, for Epic itself to review.

All documents in the sample will be drawn from the files of the seven Apple custodians referenced in Epic’s original motion.

Apple, by contrast, had suggested a considerably smaller sample of 383 documents, arguing that this would be statistically significant at a 95% confidence level.

In his decision, Judge Hixson agreed that Epic had legitimate reasons to question Apple’s reasons for withholding the documents:.

Apple’s responsiveness rate is so dramatically low that it raises red flags. With Apple screening out more than 99% of the documents that hit on the agreed search terms, it is unreasonable to ask Epic to believe that Apple is making these responsiveness calls in good faith. That is particularly true in this case, in which Judge Gonzalez Rogers has sanctioned Apple for its large-scale abuse of the attorney-client privilege for the purpose of obscuring the evidence.

Judge Hixson also rejected Apple’s suggestion that a Special Master conduct the review, arguing that given the level of familiarity with the case required to assess the relevance of these documents, Epic was the only practical option for determining whether Apple had systematically misclassified them.

Realistically, the only person who has the practical ability to determine if Apple has been systematically mis-coding documents as nonresponsive is its opponent, Epic.

In his decision, the judge agreed with Apple that the manufacturer should be allowed to review the documents for privileged and sensitive information before producing them to Epic, and authorized Apple to designate all documents produced as part of the exercise as Attorneys’ Eyes Only.

Importantly, Judge Hixson has not yet determined whether Apple systematically misclassified responsive documents as nonresponsive, nor has he imposed the daily monetary sanctions originally requested by Epic.

Apple now has until December 8 to complete the document production, with Epic having until December 15 to file any objections, and Apple until December 22 to respond.

#3216. A month with the iPhone Duo has changed how I use my phone

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2420 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

A month with the iPhone Duo has changed how I use my phone

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2420 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, for years, the definition of a premium smartphone depended on its cameras, processors, and how light it felt when you stowed it in your pocket.
  • In a little under a month of using the Duo, I’ve found that the trade-offs I was initially concerned about matter far less to me than I had expected.
  • I also easily forgot a number of my initial concerns about switching to the Duo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, for years, the definition of a premium smartphone depended on its cameras, processors, and how light it felt when you stowed it in your pocket. The iPhone Duo challenges that concept by asking consumers to pay more for a fundamentally different smartphone experience, even if it means sacrificing what they’ve long thought of as high-end features.

In a little under a month of using the Duo, I’ve found that the trade-offs I was initially concerned about matter far less to me than I had expected. What’s been more interesting is how the Duo’s foldable form factor has changed my everyday habits, including how I interact with apps, which apps I use, and how I organize and personalize the phone itself.

I also easily forgot a number of my initial concerns about switching to the Duo. The apps, for the most part, are now optimized for the Duo; I’ve reacquainted myself with Touch ID; and I don’t miss the Pro Max camera on most days.

Sources indicate that that’s not to say the Duo doesn’t have its shortcomings. I still miss that telephoto lens sometimes, and I’m still longing for Face ID — though not as much since Apple shipped a face unlock feature in the latest update. But after a month of using the Duo, I’ve found these compromises have had less of an impact on my day-to-day experience compared with the benefits that the newly introduced form factor brings.

I was surprised by how much I’ve grown to appreciate the Duo’s multitasking capabilities. Initially, I didn’t think I’d regularly use it to view two apps side by side, given the still fairly limited screen space even while the phone is unfolded, especially compared with an iPad. But I’ve found myself snapping apps to both halves of the screen more often than I had imagined.

For starters, Apple has made this side-by-side mode incredibly intuitive and easy to use — you simply drag the app over to the left or right side of the screen and drop it into the target box that appears.

I have regularly taken advantage of this feature to do all sorts of things.

In a recent development, I really enjoy keeping X open as I read through the news, which allows me to switch back and forth between the article I’m reading and real-time reactions to it. Sometimes I’ll keep email or Slack open on the side while I’m working on something else so I don’t miss an crucial message or notification.

And much like the overstimulated members of Gen Z (which I am not), I sometimes like scrolling social media while engaging with some other media off to the side.

Case in point: I passively watched Netflix’s “Love is Blind” reunion while reading the gossipy tweets and Reddit posts about the main characters on the other side of the screen. This sort of TV watching behavior used to be called second-screen viewing, but now it’s morphing into something new. Everything is happening on one screen, so should we call it “Duo screen viewing,” perhaps? It makes me long for even more interactive TV experiences where commentary and content are combined.

In a recent development, I’ve noticed another shift in my behavior since adopting the Duo as my main device. When I’m out and about, the Duo feels more like an (arguably heavier) iPhone mini. For those who still miss smaller iPhones, the Duo is the next best thing. Despite its weight, the phone feels small. You can cover it with one hand; you can type with a thumb; you can reach the top and bottom easily; and you can even fit it into your front and back pockets. The Pro Max now feels unbelievably strange in my hand — how was I ever comfortable wrangling this giant rectangle?

Industry observers note that the Duo’s small screen works well when you’re on the go, especially for short interactions like responding to a quick text or pulling up directions to a destination. It’s not as great for mindless scrolling, which I appreciate, as it forces me to engage with the real world instead of killing every moment of boredom or unease by opening up apps.

Recent findings suggest that but when you’re home or somewhere with time to kill, you can unfold the screen and enjoy your apps super-sized. It’s the best of both worlds.

Industry observers note that I find that I instinctively unfold the phone when I’m preparing to watch videos, because the larger screen is best for that. It’s also unfolded if I’m shopping, as it’s more convenient for looking at products, zooming in to examine the details, or complete checkout forms.

Generally, I also unfold the Duo when I’m actively using apps. This setup has also allowed me to rethink my Home Screen layout: With the Duo closed, I prefer to see just widgets on the small screen with key information like weather, time, battery life, and so on. Meanwhile, the only app icons on the Home Screen are those in the dock.

In the weeks since its launch, most of the apps that weren’t yet optimized for the Duo have been upgraded to support its foldable form factor. In mid-November, Apple said there were over 200,000 Duo-ready apps, and in my experience, that certainly feels true. A majority of my so-called “daily drivers” — with the glaring exception of key Google apps like Gmail and Drive — have dropped the black band on the side of the screen that was frustrating early testers of the phone.

Most apps now take advantage of the available space, whether that’s on the Duo’s small front screen or the wider, unfolded one.

I’ve also found it interesting to see the different interpretations developers have had for how to best optimize their app for Duo.

Some have used the form factor as a way to bring in some sort of novelty: there’s a note-taking app that opens and closes like a notebook, with pages you can write on with the Apple Pencil; a retro Walkman-like music player; a tiny typewriter; a gaming handheld; a game where you close the phone to make grilled cheese.

Industry observers note that as much as I love the whimsy of this group of apps, I appreciate how my everyday apps feel better to use on the unfolded screen. Spotify, at last, feels less cluttered when it has more screen real estate. A number of note-taking, list-making, and calendar apps also feel somehow more usable when spread out.

The Netflix app is actually fantastic with its support for multiple viewing modes, which include playing video on the closed outer display, the “laptop” orientation with its major player controls, and the “tent” mode.

Other developers have similarly reimagined how their app would work if it had originally been designed for the Duo’s small and larger screens.

Recent findings suggest that one good example of this is Sofa, a handy utility for organizing the books, movies, TV shows, podcasts, albums, and games you want to check out. When the Duo is closed, its navigation is tucked off to the right side in a vertical bar, while the main screen focuses on the items you’ve saved. But when the Duo is unfolded, the number of items displayed on the screen also expands into a two-column layout, with more of your items featured on the screen and your lists on the left side. It doesn’t feel like two different apps, but like you’ve opened up the app itself and given it more space to spread out.

According to recent reports, in terms of your daily social media scroll, apps like TikTok and Instagram have been updated to be perfectly usable on the Duo, whether the phone is open or closed. When closed, TikTok now stretches the video to cover the screen, instead of showing the ugly black bar. Scrolling short-form videos on the Duo, while unfolded like a slightly smaller iPad mini, has become my preferred way to watch.

Recent findings suggest that here’s another surprise: I’ve spent less time with my Kindle, and am instead reading books on my Duo. Unfolded, the Duo is a decent enough replacement for an e-book reader, albeit it can be a bit more stimulating as it’s not an e-ink device. However, the matte inner screen isn’t quite as bright and distracting as your typical glossy OLED display. There’s less glare and softer reflections, but there’s also something about the display that just feels calmer than a smartphone, allowing you to more fully engage with a book’s text.

Unfolded and held vertically, reading on the Duo feels a lot like reading on the standard Kindle, at least in terms of hand-feel. And putting your phone into the “Do Not Disturb” focus mode can help you not be distracted by incoming notifications and messages while you read.

Recent findings suggest that you can also unfold the device while keeping it in landscape orientation, with the screens bent slightly inward like a real book. For even more fun, you can turn on Kindle’s page-turn animation, which makes it seem as if you’re turning the page in a physical book. And I love how you can “performatively read” using an app like Book2Life or Actually Read — they display the book’s cover on the Duo’s outer screen as you read the text on the inner screen.

In a recent development, E-book readers will likely find they can carry one less device when they’re out and about, because the Duo can stand in for whatever Kindle or other reader you typically keep in your purse or bag. You can save the Kindle for other times, whether that’s at home, on long travel days, or when you don’t want to worry about sand getting into your $2,000 phone.

On the significant-screened iPhone 17 Pro Max I used to carry, I tended to keep a PopSocket of some sort on the back because the phone was both heavy and large, which made it hard to hold for longer periods of time. The Duo is similarly heavy, but its shape makes it far easier to hold in one hand without the extra help.

Folded, you can do the usual one-handed hold where the bottom edge of the phone rests on your pinky, your other three fingers cradle the back, and your thumb is free to navigate the screen.

Unfolded, the Duo’s like using a small Kindle or iPad mini, where two hands are required. You also don’t need a PopSocket for balancing the phone on the side, because it can be propped up like a tent or opened like a tiny laptop. Or, if you prefer, Apple and others offer Duo cases with a built-in stand. (Apple’s case comes in navy and taupe, though, so if you’re not boring, you’ll probably want to shop from third-party vendors).

If you think you still might need a PopSocket at times, or you just aren’t ready to give it up, the brand now makes a slimmer version: its Low-Pro Grip. There are other competitors, like the OhSnap grips, which aren’t a bad alternative either.

There’s something about the Duo that seems to have kicked off a new iPhone personalization trend, at least judging by what I’ve been seeing on social media.

Unlike a regular iPhone, where every phone case is simply a shell that offers a degree of protection based on the materials used, the Duo case lineup provides far more variety.

You can buy cases with and without built-in screen protectors, and some use adhesive to better stick to the outer screen, while others don’t. Some cases let you customize the band around the outer screen with a different color than the case that protects the rest of the phone.

Then you have cases that cover the hinge, while others leave it exposed. There are cases that offer holes where you can attach straps, wristlets, and charms. Some of those have attachment points at the bottom and others on the side.

Essentially, there are a lot of options for customizing how you want to carry the Duo and how you want to express your own style.

I’m also now starting to see whimsical cases that come with attached pens. (Thank goodness — most of the pen cases so far have been kind of plain!).

It has been revealed that I also believe there’s something about the Duo that particularly appeals to women. Maybe because it’s small, or maybe it’s because you can attach a strap to its side and carry it like a little purse. Or maybe because, like a purse, you can deck it out with chains and charms — a choice that’s grown increasingly popular as young people have embraced whimsical, retro tech as a way to express their individuality and sense of fashion.

In a recent development, the Duo easily lends itself to this trend, perhaps even more than a regular iPhone. It becomes an accessory you want on display, not one buried in a bag.

Before switching to the Duo, I spent a lot of time thinking about what I’d be giving up by moving away from the Pro Max.

According to recent reports, I’m surprised to find that, a month later, I only think about what I’d have to give up if I switched back to a traditional iPhone. It’s not just the extra space of the unfolded screen I’d miss — it’s all the little habits I’ve developed around having different screen sizes for different purposes.

Industry observers note that the Duo makes me pause and think about how I want to use an app. That small moment of deliberation, before I even open the phone, has helped me break some of my more mindless smartphone habits, particularly around social media.

That’s not a benefit I could have anticipated if I’d judged the device by its specifications alone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

David Anthony Sanchez scammed victims out of $260,000 worth of cryptocurrency.

A Florida man who is known as "Dave the Jewler" has been sentenced to 47 months in prison after running a cryptocurrency scam that involved using AI to impersonate a well-known streamer. David Anthony Sanchez, who pleaded guilty to money laundering and aggravated identity theft, was also ordered to pay restitution to the victims.

Industry observers note that as spotted by Aftermath, the US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida said Sanchez used AI to clone the voice of Mikyle "N3on" Rafiq in order to convince the people behind a memecoin project that the streamer had agreed to endorse, promote and take part in their scheme. The scammer pretended to be both N3on and the streamer's representative while communicating with the project's organizers.

Sanchez fooled them into transferring around $260,000 worth of cryptocurrency to accounts he controlled. He then converted some of the crypto into US dollars that he used for his personal benefit.

"Behind every fraud scheme are real people who suffer real financial harm," Yara Lorenzo Klukas, acting US Attorney for the Southern District of Florida, noted. "In this case, the defendant exploited artificial intelligence to manipulate the trust of unsuspecting victims and deprive them of their money. Today's sentence reflects our commitment to protecting victims, safeguarding the integrity of our financial markets and holding accountable those who exploit emerging technologies to defraud others.".

According to recent reports, N3on's not exactly a stranger to AI clones of himself, as it happens. Aftermath noted that he tried using a deepfake of himself to keep his Kick stream going around the clock. N3on's likeness was also used in an AI-generated movie that was released a few months ago.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union will continue to organize, however.
  • Rockstar Games workers in the UK have overwhelmingly voted against a union recognition effort, with three-quarters rejecting an agreement with the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union.
  • In a recent development, over 93 percent of Rockstar workers across offices in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee and London took part in the two-week ballot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union will continue to organize, however.

Rockstar Games workers in the UK have overwhelmingly voted against a union recognition effort, with three-quarters rejecting an agreement with the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union. The vote took place at the same time the company released Grand Theft Auto 6, which smashed records as it generated $3.79 billion in pre-orders and first-day sales.

In a recent development, over 93 percent of Rockstar workers across offices in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee and London took part in the two-week ballot. Of those, 1,163 turned down formal recognition of their branch of the IWGB (Independent Workers Union of Great Britain), while 381 were in favor, according to IGN.

Industry observers note that the Rockstar Game Workers Union will continue to organize without a formal agreement with the organization. However, the result means Rockstar management won't be obligated to officially recognize the union or hold regular meetings with representatives.

Recent findings suggest that "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society — this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for," the union stated in a statement. "Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We're ready to put in the effort to make that happen." It added that it will keep battling for "pay transparency, contractual overtime pay and protections against AI and layoffs.".

In a recent development, "We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6," Jennifer Kolbe, Rockstar Games head of publishing, said in a statement. "This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together.".

Rockstar had indicated a willingness to work with its workers on unionization. "We go where the team goes," Klobe told Bloomberg for a story about the making of GTA 6. "So if they want a union, they will have a union.".

In October last year, Rockstar fired dozens of workers, claiming they had shared confidential details about GTA 6 and made disparaging remarks about the company. The IWGB issued formal legal claims against Rockstar in which it accused the Take-Two subsidiary of union busting and unlawfully firing those workers. An employment tribunal heard closing evidence last week and a final judgement in the case is pending.

Readdle updated its Documents app for iPhone and iPad this week with Voice Notes, a new AI-powered feature that lets owners record conversations and automatically generate transcripts, summaries, and follow-up notes. Here are the details.

While the habit of recording meetings, lectures, or even one’s own thoughts is not particularly newly introduced, modern AI tools and models have made it considerably easier to extract useful information from these recordings without having to listen back to them in their entirety or take copious notes that can distract from the actual conversation.

This week, Readdle’s Documents introduced Voice Notes, which “lets you record audio and turn it into a summary, follow-ups, and a full transcript,” as the manufacturer put it.

Consumers can start a upcoming recording session by tapping the “+” button in the app and selecting Voice Notes. Alternatively, they can start recording from the iPhone’s Action button, which is a nice touch.

Once they’re done, Readdle notes Documents can generate:.

People can cycle through these three tabs, where they can also listen to the original recording or copy and share the information.

Readdle claims Voice Notes can recognize multiple languages in the same conversation, with the actual transcript preserving the languages as spoken, “while the summary and follow-ups are generated in the most frequently spoken language.”.

Each voice note is saved as a single file in Documents that contains the original recording, transcript, summary, and follow-ups. Customers can organize these files into folders, share them, sync them with their cloud storage, and save the transcript as a separate .txt file.

However, if users give a voice note’s AI-generated content a thumbs down, Readdle may retain its transcript and summary for up to six months, or until the user objects to their processing, whichever comes first.

The company also notes user data isn’t used to train AI models, although third-party AI providers may retain inputs for up to 30 days for abuse and misuse monitoring, or longer if required by law.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Companies like Dell have stopped shipping server hardware to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.
  • Sources indicate that NVIDIA has reportedly put a stop to shipments of AI server hardware to four Southeast Asian countries.
