📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Companies like Dell have stopped shipping server hardware to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.

Sources indicate that NVIDIA has reportedly put a stop to shipments of AI server hardware to four Southeast Asian countries. According to The Financial Times, a handful of the organization's manufacturing partners, including Dell and Supermicro, told clients in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia that the chipmaker is not allowing their server orders to be sent to them. The Financial Times reports it's unclear if the halt is temporary. The news comes just days after NVIDIA reinstated Jensen Huang as its chief executive.

Sources indicate that in recent years, Chinese AI labs have turned to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia to gain access to NVIDIA's most powerful chips. They used a gap in US export controls by renting access through cloud compute providers that bought servers with NVIDIA GPUs inside. In recent weeks, the US Commerce Department moved to close that loophole. First by introducing fresh rules aimed at stopping that exact practice, and second by targeting Megaspeed, the manufacturer at the center of the NVIDIA scandal.

It has been revealed that on Wednesday, the Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its "Entity List." Companies, including NVIDIA, now need a US license to ship goods covered by US export rules to Megaspeed. Huang had resigned from his position on November 12 after reports surfaced that he had engaged in multiple extramarital affairs, including one involving Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive that some US officials suspect was a Chinese intelligence asset. Megaspeed had leased access to NVIDIA chips to Chinese companies. The Justice Department is also investigating whether Megaspeed broke US export rules.

It has been revealed that under the newly introduced US rule, data centers that were already providing large amounts of computing power to companies based in China or other location covered by the rule have 90 days from November 19 to get a license if they want to keep doing so. "There's this new rule but no guidance on execution," one cloud executive told the outlet. "No one knows how to apply for this license while the 90-day clock is ticking. It's causing sheer chaos in the region." Demand from Chinese tech companies led to a data center construction boom in Southeast Asia. NVIDIA booked $104 billion in revenue through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, representing a 72 percent increase from the year before.

X finally gets parental controls after 20 years

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After 20 years of existence, X, the social network formerly known as Twitter, has finally added parental controls for teenagers, giving parents and guardians a way to manage what their kids see and interact with on the platform.
  • Industry observers note that the organization noted accounts belonging to 13-to-17-year-olds will be set to “protected mode” by default, meaning they won’t be able to see sensitive content, and won’t be served targeted ads.
  • The controls let parents see how much time their teen spends on X per week, set daily limits, require their approval for new followers, limit feed recommendations and videos to already followed accounts, filter specific words, turn off sensitive media, specify who can send their teen DMs, and see who they are messaging.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After 20 years of existence, X, the social network formerly known as Twitter, has finally added parental controls for teenagers, giving parents and guardians a way to manage what their kids see and interact with on the platform. But unlike most platforms’ implementation of such controls, X is putting its own spin on the system by giving teens a say in the matter.

Industry observers note that the organization noted accounts belonging to 13-to-17-year-olds will be set to “protected mode” by default, meaning they won’t be able to see sensitive content, and won’t be served targeted ads. However, X is allowing teenagers to retain a measure of control over their accounts, letting them see what restrictions were made to their accounts. Parents and guardians will also not be able to read their teens’ private messages, see search or viewing history, or post as their teen.

The controls let parents see how much time their teen spends on X per week, set daily limits, require their approval for new followers, limit feed recommendations and videos to already followed accounts, filter specific words, turn off sensitive media, specify who can send their teen DMs, and see who they are messaging.

The controls arrive months after X came under fire for a lack of controls preventing the platform’s AI chatbot from being used to generate sexualized images of children and women. The social network has also long been rife with child sexual abuse material, misinformation, AI bots, and openly lets users post porn.

Recent findings suggest that X has generally not been a platform aimed at teenagers, but that doesn’t mean they don’t use the platform. A 2024 study found that nearly a third of Gen Alpha kids have an X account. The platform itself requires people to be at least 13 years old, though that’s not a high bar given the kind of content on the platform.

It has been revealed that “Parents want practical tools, and teens deserve room to grow. With Parental Controls on X, families can set the guardrails that fit their home, while teens keep ownership of their accounts and can see every change. Striking that balance is vital and what we set out to build.” Michael O’Herlihy, head of safety at X, wrote in a blog post.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Protests are planned in Los Angeles and Chicago, while a union called for strikes at 11 Amazon sites in Germany.

Amazon workers and their supporters are once again set to go on strike and hold protests in more than 20 countries across the Black Friday and Cyber Monday period. Trade union federation UNI Global remarked the workers are pushing Amazon to negotiate with unions and respect employees' right to organize.

Industry observers note that teamsters are planning protests on Cyber Monday (November 30) in Los Angeles and Chicago. "As part of a global day of action, Amazon workers are demanding fair wages, safer working conditions, union recognition and respect on the job," a local Teamsters union representing workers in Southern California said.

German trade union Verdi called strikes at 11 Amazon sites on Black Friday (November 27). It claimed the wages the organization pays often aren't enough for workers to live on and that warehouse work puts a "considerable physical strain on employees." According to Deutsche Presse-Agentur, Verdi also stated Amazon uses digital trackers to keep close tabs on around 40,000 employees. An Amazon spokesman denied Verdi's claims and said average starting pay was above the German minimum wage.

Industry observers note that amazon workers and their allies are also set to mobilize in Canada, Australia, India, Bangladesh, Poland, Luxembourg, Brazil, Colombia, Uruguay, Indonesia, Japan, the Philippines, Thailand, Fiji, Singapore, South Africa and elsewhere. UNI Global said this is the seventh year of the Make Amazon Pay campaign, which it convenes alongside Progressive International.

In a recent development, "The fact is at Amazon we provide great pay, great benefits and great opportunities — all from day one," an Amazon spokesperson told Engadget in a statement. "We directly employ more than 1.5 million people around the world, and provide a modern, safe and engaging workplace whether you work in an office or at one of our operations buildings.".

Earlier this month, workers at a warehouse in Delta, British Columbia, became the first in North America to win a union contract with Amazon. The terms of the three-year pact were imposed through binding arbitration. Among other things, the contract ensures pay increases (up to $29 CAD per hour by the time it ends), an extra week of vacation for workers with 10 years of service and severance of up to 18 weeks.

British Columbia's labor relations board ordered arbitration in August despite Amazon's objections. After an arbitrator imposed the agreement, Amazon vice-president J. Ofori Agboka remarked the process was "improper [and] unfair" and that it "defies common sense," adding that the organization would take the matter to court if need be.

In April, the NLRB ordered Amazon to recognize and bargain with a union at the JFK8 warehouse on Staten Island, Fresh York. The company is contesting the order. JFK8 workers voted to unionize in 2022, becoming the first Amazon warehouse in the US to do so.

In a recent development, yesterday, we covered a Counterpoint Research report on Q3 Latin American smartphone shipments, which demonstrated Apple recording the smallest year-over-year decline among the region’s top five smartphone makers. As a result, Apple increased its share of regional shipments from 7% to 9%.

Apple, by contrast, kept iPhone pricing largely stable for much of the year, holding off on broader price increases until the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro lineup in September.

Today, Counterpoint Research released its report on US smartphone shipments for Q3, which showed that Apple increased its share from 50% to 57% year over year, amid a 9% decline in overall shipments.

According to a separate Counterpoint report published last Thursday, Apple was the only major smartphone maker to avoid a year-over-year decline in shipment volume during the quarter.

Sources indicate that in today’s report, Counterpoint notes that rising memory costs hit the low-end Android segment particularly hard during the quarter. Samsung was the only major Android smartphone maker to increase its shipment share, seeing a one-percentage-point bump to 25%, “helped by a portfolio spanning flagships and the low-end Galaxy A-series.”.

Carriers also felt the impact of the broader downturn, with smartphone sales across the three major US carriers collectively falling 4% year over year, per the report.

Looking ahead, Counterpoint expects memory costs to remain elevated and US carriers to be more selective with their holiday promotions, with smartphone sales expected to remain weak in Q4 despite it typically being the strongest quarter of the year.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The central, still-unproven claim in the Nvidia scandal is that Alice Huang, a former executive at the data-center tech giant Megaspeed, is a Chinese spy.
  • Industry observers note that what’s publicly known is murkier than the headlines suggest.
  • According to recent reports, undisputed reporting demonstrates the claim emerged from the White House itself.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The central, still-unproven claim in the Nvidia scandal is that Alice Huang, a former executive at the data-center tech giant Megaspeed, is a Chinese spy. She had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who abruptly resigned on Nov. 12 after acknowledging it and was just as abruptly reinstated on Monday of this week.

Industry observers note that what’s publicly known is murkier than the headlines suggest. U.S. intelligence has reportedly tracked Alice Huang’s contact with an officer of China’s spy agency, but officials haven’t offered public evidence that she was commissioned to target Nvidia’s chief. In the past week, after President Trump successfully pushed to bring Jensen Huang back, the administration has played down the allegations it once circulated internally. Whether that reflects upcoming intelligence or political pressure is the major question.

According to recent reports, undisputed reporting demonstrates the claim emerged from the White House itself. It first appeared in a highly classified memo written in March under the oversight of Secretary of State Marco Rubio and circulated to White House officials ahead of Trump’s trip to China in May. The memo formed the partial basis for the Newly introduced York Times’ initial reporting on the scandal, published Oct. 29 and its existence was first reported on Nov. 8.

Industry observers note that the memo did not definitively say, according to the Wall Street Journal, that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. CNN, by contrast, has reported that the memo concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset.

What’s better established is that Alice Huang was in touch with Chinese intelligence. The Ministry of State Security (MSS) is Beijing’s civilian spy agency, responsible for both foreign intelligence and domestic counterintelligence. Last weekend, the Times, citing people with knowledge of U.S. intelligence reports, reported that Huang was in contact with an MSS officer from the spring of 2025 until this fall, a period that overlaps her relationship with Jensen Huang. (The Chinese government has called the spy claims a “smear,” and Megaspeed indicates Huang left the company in August 2025 and that its business is legitimate.).

Top Trump officials have nonetheless all but discredited the espionage claims, along with the suggestion that Nvidia fell prey to spying or foreign influence.

In a recent development, attorney General Todd Blanche, who was Trump’s personal defense lawyer before taking over the Justice Department, told journalists on Tuesday: “I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen.” On the same day, Trump noted a pardon was an option for Jensen Huang but that he did not think one would be needed. Senior intelligence officials reportedly told Congress that the government apparently has no actual evidence that the MSS directed Alice Huang to pursue an affair with Jensen Huang.

According to recent reports, none of those statements necessarily exonerates Alice Huang as an intelligence agent. Instead, they support the alternate theory that the Chinese government didn’t tell her to begin the affair and that Jensen Huang broke no law by having it. Not being directed to have an affair isn’t the same as not being a spy, though.

According to recent reports, from a certain angle, the circumstantial evidence surrounding Alice Huang looks quite suspicious. She was a top executive at a tech giant investigated for illicitly channeling Nvidia chips to China, and her husband, Kang Wei, is noted to have even closer ties to the MSS, with some sources saying he worked for the agency.

In a recent development, the timing of the government’s reversal is at the heart of the matter. Trump has stated he lobbied the board “directly and indirectly” to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, so it wouldn’t be surprising if officials who serve at his pleasure were recasting the case in terms that satisfy his agenda. That wouldn’t necessarily make their assessments wrong. But unless new intelligence has actually resolved the question, and none has been publicly identified as yet, that backdrop is critical to keep in mind. CBS has also reported that Rubio, whose office oversaw the original memo, has privately voiced concerns about aspects of Jensen Huang’s return.

Doubts persist elsewhere, too. Earlier this month, CNN reported that the intelligence community was still working to understand Alice Huang’s relationship with Jensen Huang and that the intelligence collected on her to date does not prove she was acting as a spy for Beijing. After a briefing by top intelligence officials earlier this month, Rep. Jim Himes (D-Conn.), the incoming chair of the House Intelligence Committee, said he was unsure whether she was a spy or a “useful idiot.” And this week, the Wall Street Journal pointed out that under Chinese leader Xi Jinping, top corporate executives routinely maintain ties to the country’s intelligence service without being formally deputized as assets.

In a recent development, the crush of conflicting claims, most from anonymous government sources, obviously leaves large questions unanswered as to what actually transpired. Some of those questions that naturally spring to mind:.

According to recent reports, there are answers to all of these questions, of course, but when the public will get them is anybody’s guess. Jensen Huang is due to appear before the Senate Banking Committee next week, and by the look from the statements of some of its members, he’s likely in for a rough ride. Unfortunately, congressional hearings, particularly public ones, rarely unearth secrets that haven’t already been disclosed.

Industry News: 1Password says it was hacked but owners' vaults are safe

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The attacker wasn't able to access people's vaults.
  • Sources indicate that 1Password has admitted that an attacker was able to infiltrate its system and steal some customer data, but it has assured users in its announcement that their vaults and logins are safe.
  • Sources indicate that the attacker was then able to download customers' data, including people's names and email addresses, the dates their accounts were created and their last sign-in times.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The attacker wasn't able to access people's vaults.

Sources indicate that 1Password has admitted that an attacker was able to infiltrate its system and steal some customer data, but it has assured users in its announcement that their vaults and logins are safe. On November 19, the firm started investigating signs that an employee's corporate GitHub account had been compromised. The company found that the attacker used that account to access its source code and inject malicious code to its backend.

Sources indicate that the attacker was then able to download customers' data, including people's names and email addresses, the dates their accounts were created and their last sign-in times. They were also able to steal users' public keys, but 1Password remarked it has no impact to their security. While the bad actor was also able to steal source code from the company itself, it doesn't contain customer data.

It has been revealed that "Your vault data, the items in them, and the keys that protect them are safe and were not affected," 1Password wrote. The service doesn't have access to consumers' actual passwords, recovery keys and other credentials, as well as the secret keys that protect their vaults, so the attacker wasn't able to steal them. Since discovering the breach, 1Password has revoked the stolen token, disabled the affected GitHub account and added new detection tools for similar attacks.

Sources indicate that while 1Password remarked that users' vaults remain safe, the company still advises being vigilant when it comes to phishing attempts. It warned that since users' emails were compromised in the breach, they could be used in attempts to grab people's passwords through fake account recovery and invitation emails.

Latest Update: Ford unveils the GT41 as it hopes to win Le Mans again

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (492 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sixty years ago, after two failed attempts, Ford won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with its GT40 race car.
  • “Revealing the Ford GT41 is a significant moment for everyone involved in this program,” said Dan Sayers, manager of Ford Racing’s Hypercar program.
  • Recent findings suggest that like many other entrants in the World Endurance Championship’s Hypercar class, Ford has chosen the rear-wheel-drive LMDh technical approach rather than building the GT41 entirely from scratch, as Ferrari and Aston Martin do with their cars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sixty years ago, after two failed attempts, Ford won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with its GT40 race car. In the years since, the Blue Oval has been back to France more than a few times, with varying success. It could never replicate the GT40’s success winning overall, but it celebrated the 40th anniversary with a class win. Now it wants another shot at the really big trophy, and it debuted the car during the Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears football game today: meet the GT41.

“Revealing the Ford GT41 is a significant moment for everyone involved in this program,” said Dan Sayers, manager of Ford Racing’s Hypercar program. “It’s the result of an enormous amount of work across our engineering, design, and development teams and an notable milestone on our journey towards 2027. We know the scale of the challenge ahead—the level of competition in Hypercar is incredibly high, and there are no shortcuts to success. Our focus has been on building the right foundations, bringing together the right people and making sure we learn as much as possible from every stage of development.”.

Recent findings suggest that like many other entrants in the World Endurance Championship’s Hypercar class, Ford has chosen the rear-wheel-drive LMDh technical approach rather than building the GT41 entirely from scratch, as Ferrari and Aston Martin do with their cars. LMDh cars start with one of four approved carbon fiber chassis—in this case, Ford is working with Oreca, which has also partnered with Genesis and Acura.

Sources indicate that the hybrid system and transmission are also standard parts. But Ford supplies the engine—a 5.4 L V8 based on the Mustang’s Coyote engine—as well as software to control the hybrid powertrain. A non-hybridized version of the Coyote has already been racing effectively under the hood of the Ford Mustang GT3.

The technical regulations also allow for more styling freedom than we often see in racing. The absolute amount of aerodynamic downforce is capped, as is the minimum drag, so OEMs are encouraged to use road car styling details to create a closer link between prototype and road car. I’ll probably need to spend more time looking at it to spot those road car cues, but I do see quite a few superficial similarities with the Genesis LMDh car, as well as the Ferrari Hypercar.

Sources indicate that despite being an American car brand, Ford doesn’t have aims as yet to enter IMSA’s WeatherTech championship, so don’t expect to see the GT41 next January racing at Daytona. Instead, it will take its first green flag in Qatar in March, the first of WEC’s nine races next season.

Ford should find it an extremely competitive championship. Although Peugeot and Alpine will not race next year, McLaren is also entering, alongside returning teams from Aston Martin, BMW, Cadillac, Genesis, Ferrari, and Toyota, which this year won Le Mans and the overall title, following three years of Ferrari domination.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh season of Midnight Diner: Tokyo Stories is streaming now, though it’s easy to miss.

A latest season of Midnight Diner: Tokyo Stories is streaming now, though it’s easy to miss.

It has been revealed that the bigger Netflix gets, the easier it is to miss stuff. This is true of all digital platforms, of course, but it’s especially true of Netflix of late, as the streaming service’s lineup now also includes a growing library of reality indicates, live-programming, and even games. It makes it easy for some of the best shows to zoom right past you, unnoticed — which almost happened to me with Midnight Diner.

If you haven’t seen it, Midnight Diner is probably the most comforting thing available on Netflix. The show follows the patrons of a cozy little restaurant tucked away in the backstreets of Shinjuku, which is only open during the unusual hours of midnight to 7:00AM. This, in turn, attracts a unique blend of customers, who help each other out under the watchful eye of the shop’s owner (Kaoru Kobayashi), known only as “master.” The show aired for three seasons on Japanese TV, before being picked up by Netflix for a handful more under the subtitle Tokyo Stories.

Industry observers note that what’s especially notable about the show’s return is the huge gap: season 2 of the Netflix iteration streamed in 2019, and it took seven years for it to come back. The break was so long that season 3’s first episode, which premiered in October, is about the restaurant’s struggles during the pandemic. There are a bunch of cute scenes of the diner’s regulars sneaking outside to check if the restaurant is open yet, and wondering if it will ever be able to. If nothing else, the break was a chance for the reliable master to finally take a vacation.

But once Midnight Diner’s newly introduced season gets going, it’s right back to everything that made it beloved. Each episode uses a different dish as a way of exploring a particular story. An overworked manga artist imagines the life he missed out on over plates of spicy konjac, while a pair of old friends reconnect while munching on pork cutlet sandwiches. What’s remarkable about the show is the way it balances being a charming, comforting watch with exploring truly difficult and heartbreaking topics. It’s the combination of sweetness and sadness that makes it work so well. It’s as likely to make you laugh as it is to make you cry.

And unlike most Netflix series, the whole season isn’t streaming all at once. Instead, new episodes come out every Tuesday; so far six of a planned 10 episodes are available. It’s a welcome way to spend an evening, as the show’s slow pace and warm sense of humanity can feel like all-too rare traits in the current streaming landscape.

Sources indicate that but the main reason I’m even writing about Midnight Diner’s return is that it has been so easy to miss. There’s been next to no promotion for it — all I could find was a trailer on Netflix’s Japanese YouTube channel — and I only happened upon it accidentally after the initial premiere while browsing aimlessly through Netflix’s new releases. This, despite being someone who has watched and rewatched the previous seasons multiple times. You’d think I’d get a notification or something. Netflix has always been full of hidden gems, but now that it’s busier than ever, those gems are all the more hidden.

It has been revealed that south Korea’s Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) announced today that it has opened formal proceedings against Apple over its advertising of Apple Intelligence features for the iPhone 16 lineup. Here are the details.

Back in March 2025, shortly after Apple confirmed it was delaying the rollout of what would eventually become Siri AI, the South Korean civic group Seoul YMCA filed a complaint with the KFTC.

At the time, Yonhap reported that the organization had previously called on Apple to compensate affected customers, and alleged that the organization may have continued to market the iPhone 16 lineup despite already knowing that some of its advertised AI features would be delayed.

As 9to5Mac readers will likely remember, Apple widely advertised Apple Intelligence and AI-powered Siri features as part of its iPhone 16 launch campaign, going so far as to give its iconic Fifth Avenue store an Apple Intelligence-themed makeover and run an ad campaign starring Bella Ramsey.

It has been revealed that this landed Apple in legal and regulatory trouble in multiple markets, including the US, where the company agreed to a $250 million class action settlement earlier this year, and Brazil, where it came under scrutiny from a consumer protection agency in May. Now, the company is facing potential penalties in South Korea as well.

As a result of Seoul YMCA’s complaint, the KFTC conducted an investigation into Apple’s advertising practices. Today, the regulator declared (via MacRumors) that its investigators had submitted their findings and recommendations for formal deliberation by the Commission.

According to the KFTC’s press release, investigators concluded that Apple advertised Apple Intelligence and its planned staggered rollout on the iPhone 16 website, but “concealed, downplayed, or omitted information material to consumers’ purchasing decisions.”.

That included, per the press release (translation ours):.

The press release also notes that Genmoji, Image Playground, “Siri with the ability to understand personal context,” and “Siri that provides step-by-step guidance” were not made available as advertised:.

For example, Siri’s ability to understand personal context was advertised as being scheduled to launch first in US English by the end of 2024, as currently available in US English in October 2024, and as scheduled to support Korean in early April 2025.

In reality, the feature was not debuted in US English until September 2026, with Korean language support following in October 2026.

As a result, the investigators concluded that Apple’s conduct constituted a violation of the country’s Labeling and Advertising Act, which prohibits deceptive labeling and advertising.

They recommended issuing corrective orders, including a prohibition on such conduct in the future, as well as imposing a financial penalty.

They also estimate that Apple’s revenue associated with the alleged violation amounts to approximately 3.35 trillion South Korean won (roughly $2.5 billion), though the KFTC’s press release does not specify the amount of the fine.

⁠Yonhap noted today that the fine could reach roughly $48 million, while ⁠KBS reported that it could range between $21 million and $42 million.

With the report now submitted, Apple has six weeks to submit its written defense before the Commission deliberates and makes a final determination on whether the company violated the law and, if so, how much it should be fined.

In a statement to MacRumors, Apple mentioned it had cooperated with the KFTC’s investigation, but disagreed with the conclusions. The company also highlighted the rollout of Korean-language support for Apple Intelligence last year and, more recently, for Siri AI.

As for why those countries, Chinese companies have been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers there, a loophole the US Commerce Department closed — reportedly grudgingly — earlier this month. The Journal notes that the think tank Institute for Progress estimates remote data centers like these supply about 24% of China’s AI computing power.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The website does not store payment, government ID or financial information, so none of that was exposed.

Recent findings suggest that video game-logging site Backloggd has urged people to change their passwords after announcing a security breach. The website's administrator MrProg wrote in a post dated November 25 that "someone exploited a bug in Backloggd to gain access to the site's admin tools." As a result, the infiltrator was able to access usernames, email addresses, hashed passwords and the IP addresses users signed in from. Payment information was not affected as that's handled through Patreon.

Backloggd admin MrProg stated that, while the platform uses "a strong hashing method" to mask login credentials, "weak or common passwords can sometimes be guessed from their hashes." As such, it's best for Backlogged people to change their password for the site and anywhere else they use the same one. (Take this as a reminder to opt for a strong, unique password on every single service you use. A password manager can help handle that, while passkeys and multi-factor authentication add extra layers of security to your accounts.).

According to recent reports, mrProg apologized for the security incident. The admin took Backloggd offline as soon as they became aware of the situation to fix the bug and lock out the attacker, who also hid games and restricted some accounts. All users will need to log back in, and MrProg noted they're reverting all the changes the attacker made.

"Your game logs, reviews and lists all remain intact," MrProg added. "I'm currently seeking legal guidance to ensure I handle this with absolute care and will share a full notice with more details soon." The site's operator has "already added stricter access to the admin tools and will continue to commit to stronger security features to help protect your account.".

Backloggd is a site on which people can log and rate games they play, in a similar fashion to what Letterboxd does for movies. People can track their game collection, review what they've played, create lists and follow their friends' gaming progress. Backloggd has been around for eight years and it hit 1 million users this month. A native mobile app is coming next year. Those who back the site via Patreon can now check out a beta version of the Android app.

Upcoming York is banning AI chatbot toys for kids. Heres what the law covers.

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (832 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Talking dolls and stuffed animals have been holiday gifts for decades.
  • In Newly introduced York, those toys have a few more months on the shelves.
  • Hochul urged parents to think twice before buying an AI toy this holiday season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Talking dolls and stuffed animals have been holiday gifts for decades. But with the rapid adoption of AI across all industries, many of the toys on shelves today can answer questions, make up stories, and carry on full conversations with a child.

In Newly introduced York, those toys have a few more months on the shelves. On Tuesday, Nov. 24, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul signed a law banning the manufacture, distribution, and sale of children’s toys with built-in AI companions in the state for five years. The ban takes effect Feb. 22, 2027, though, so the toys can still be sold over the holidays.

Hochul urged parents to think twice before buying an AI toy this holiday season. "Parents shopping for gifts for the holidays or any other occasion should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk," she stated in a statement.

Sources indicate that A toy has to meet two definitions to fall under the ban, the first being who the toy is made for. Newly introduced York borrows a federal definition that covers products designed or intended for play by kids 12 and younger. The age printed on the box is one factor, alongside how the toy is packaged and advertised and who shoppers generally understand it to be for. That means a "13+" label alone wouldn’t settle whether a toy is covered.

The second definition is about what the toy does. Upcoming York defines an AI companion as a system designed to mimic an ongoing relationship: It remembers past conversations and preferences to personalize its responses, asks about feelings unprompted, and keeps conversations going about personal topics. A doll that simply plays a few prerecorded phrases falls outside that definition.

The state attorney general can seek civil penalties of up to $15,000 a day for each violation. Yikes!

Sources indicate that over the past year, researchers and child advocates have raised concerns about what AI toys might say to kids, what information they collect about them, and how they encourage children to see a chatbot as a friend. The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

In a recent development, last week, on Nov. 20, Mashable reported on tests of seven AI toys by U.S. PIRG, a consumer advocacy nonprofit. Two stood out (in a bad way). The Alilo Smart AI Bunny discussed sexual fetishes with a tester and suggested where to look for bleach at home, while the GoLabs AI Panda also gave sexually explicit answers.

Some toys did better than in previous tests; for example, FoloToy's Kumma teddy bear, which discussed sexual topics in last year's tests, shut down age-inappropriate prompts this year.

Recent findings suggest that after U.S. PIRG raised concerns about the AI bunny and panda last week, Amazon removed listings for both toys. Amazon told the nonprofit it had removed the listings while it investigated the safety concerns.

"Amazon is committed to the safety of children and families," the company stated in a statement to Mashable. "We're working with our partners across the industry and government to ensure proper guardrails for these products are in place as this technology develops.".

The firm also told Mashable that it requires third-party sellers to comply with applicable laws and regulations.

Three days later, on Nov. 23, a coalition of 155 child advocacy groups led by Fairplay, Alliance 4 Children CIC, and Set@16 called on the CEOs of Amazon and eBay to stop selling AI toys and offer refunds to families who had already bought them. In an open letter, the groups noted they'd found more than 50 AI toys for sale on Amazon’s U.S. marketplace, writing that, "these products should be shown to be safe before they reach children, not withdrawn one at a time after harm is found.".

In a recent development, still, about one in four U.S. parents with kids 8 and younger told Common Sense Media they already owned an AI toy or were considering buying one this holiday season. While high, these numbers are down from about half in 2025. For companies selling kids an AI friend, its clear the harder sell now may be earning their parents' trust.

Words can be made from linked letters — up, down, left, right, or diagonal, but words can also change direction, resulting in quirky shapes and patterns. Every single letter in the grid will be part of an answer. There's always a theme linking every solution, along with the "spangram," a special, word or phrase that sums up that day's theme, and spans the entire grid horizontally or vertically.

By providing an opaque hint and not providing the word list, Strands creates a brain-teasing game that takes a little longer to play than its other games, like Wordle and Connections.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • 26, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waning Gibbous phase, with 96% of its surface visible.
  • Recent findings suggest that if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Serenitatis, Kepler Crater, as well as the Tycho Crater.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Moon is still looking almost full tonight, despite being a couple of days past the Full Moon. It's now in its Waning Gibbous phase, meaning the illuminated portion we can see is gradually getting smaller each night.

As of Thursday, Nov. 26, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waning Gibbous phase, with 96% of its surface visible.

Recent findings suggest that if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Serenitatis, Kepler Crater, as well as the Tycho Crater. With binoculars, you'll also see the Gassendi Crater, the Endymion Crater, and the Posidonius Crater. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 14 and 15 landing spots, plus the Descartes Highlands.

In North America, the next Full Moon will take place on December 23. In other time zones it will fall on December 24.

In a recent development, it takes around 29.5 days for the Moon to move through all its phases, according to NASA. Throughout this period, the Moon's position relative to Earth and the Sun determines how much of its illuminated surface we can see. Starting with a Upcoming Moon, the visible portion gradually increases until it reaches a Full Moon, before shrinking again as the cycle comes back around.

Upcoming Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

Industry observers note that first Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

Recent findings suggest that waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you like playing daily word games like Wordle, then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine.

There are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown.

An important note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle.

If you find yourself stuck at any step of today's Hurdle, don't worry! We have you covered.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was returned to the job earlier this week, the board reinstating him amidst plummeting stock prices and apparent intervention from President Donald Trump. Now doubt is being cast on allegations that one of Huang's affair partners was a Chinese spy.

Huang has admitted to cheating on his wife with at least four partners as of this week, however his relationship with Alice Huang (no relation) has drawn the most scrutiny. A former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, Ms. Huang is suspected of being an intelligent agent who shared information with the Chinese government and smuggled Nvidia chips into China, circumventing U.S. restrictions.

According to recent reports, as such, Nvidia opened an independent investigation once Huang and Ms. Huang's relationship came to light, as well as established a committee to oversee the company's national security policies and export control compliance. Huang will also be interviewed by the U.S. House Foreign Affairs Committee, House Select Committee on China, and House Intelligence Committee on Dec. 1, and testify before the U.S. Senate on Dec. 3.

In a recent development, however, the Wall Street Journal and Upcoming York Times now report that the U.S. has no evidence that the Chinese government directed Ms. Huang to begin an affair with Nvidia's CEO. Instead, current evidence indicates that the pair's extramarital entanglement may have been a matter of ordinary human infidelity rather than deliberate international espionage. U.S officials reportedly informed congressional staffers of this in a briefing on Nov. 24, the day after Nvidia reinstated Huang. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile Products available for purchase through affiliate links. If you buy something through links on our site, Mashable may earn an affiliate commission.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

It has been revealed that this isn't to say that U.S. agencies didn't find any link between Ms. Huang and the Chinese government at all. U.S. officials reportedly stated that China's Ministry of State Security asked Ms. Huang to provide them with some unspecified information, which she allegedly did in accordance with Chinese law. They also claimed that her husband, businessman Kang Wei, was a Chinese intelligence asset. However, while the full extent of Ms. Huang's relationship with the Chinese government remains unclear, there is reportedly nothing to suggest that she passed on any significant information.

The Chinese government has consistently rejected claims that Ms. Huang was an intelligence agent. In an Oct. 30 press conference, Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun called such reports "unsubstantiated" and "nothing but smears against China." He later reiterated China's stance after Huang revealed his first affair on Nov. 8.

"On the so-called 'Chinese spy,' we have made our position clear," Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Mao Ning remarked in a Nov. 12 press briefing. "China's sci-tech progress relies on independent innovation and open cooperation. The U.S. should stop fabricating the 'Chinese spy' narratives as a pretext for imposing technology restrictions.".

It has been revealed that the U.S. government at the moment restricts Nvidia's chip sales to China, citing national security concerns. Several other categories of foreign-made devices are also banned from entering the U.S. due to national security, including WiFi routers and robot vacuums.

How Hinges deep-learning Most Compatible feature actually works, and how to train it

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ever since its introduction in 2018, Hinge's "Most Compatible" feature has earned equal parts praise and scorn from online daters, who can't seem to decide if it's the best thing ever or a bad joke.
  • Even today, eight years after it was first introduced, Most Compatible is a marvel of mathematical engineering, beginning with its foundation: the Gale-Shapley algorithm (also known as the propose-and-reject algorithm), developed all the way back in 1962 to solve a (hypothetical) mating problem.
  • Recent findings suggest that hinge's variation of the algorithm works dynamically, constantly taking into account user preferences and choices to predict what kind of person you would most like to date.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ever since its introduction in 2018, Hinge's "Most Compatible" feature has earned equal parts praise and scorn from online daters, who can't seem to decide if it's the best thing ever or a bad joke.

Even today, eight years after it was first introduced, Most Compatible is a marvel of mathematical engineering, beginning with its foundation: the Gale-Shapley algorithm (also known as the propose-and-reject algorithm), developed all the way back in 1962 to solve a (hypothetical) mating problem.

Recent findings suggest that hinge's variation of the algorithm works dynamically, constantly taking into account user preferences and choices to predict what kind of person you would most like to date. At the start of each upcoming day, you will receive a Most Compatible profile suggestion that expires after 24 hours unless you interact with it.

AdultFriendFinder — readers’ pick for casual connections.

Tinder — top pick for fast hookups.

Hinge — popular choice for regular meetups.

Pure — best for anonymous hookups.

OkCupid — best app for inclusivity.

But there's a massive catch here that too many Hinge users are unaware of: your own actions and inactions are factored into the equation, so if you feed the algorithm bad data, it won't work in your favor, and you'll rarely see a compelling profile suggestion. We reached out to Hinge to gain a better understanding of their algorithm from the inside, and they described it as a "recommendation system" that combines multiple algorithms, "using your stated preferences and your activity on the app," to adjust and refine its suggestions.

Here are three key tips from Hinge to help its recommendation algorithm work for you:.

Too many Hinge people (and men in particular!) cast a wide net, interacting with as many profiles as possible, sending out Likes all over the place. We get it: the more-is-more approach has its appeal, but it actually hurts the algorithm's effectiveness, since it becomes harder to narrow down your preferences when you're too indiscriminate about who you like or interact with.

Or, as Hinge told us: "If you send too many likes, we can’t tell what you truly want. At the same time, if you rarely send likes, we don’t have enough information to learn from about who excites you. By engaging with others with curiosity and purpose, your recommendations meaningfully evolve alongside you.".

Recent findings suggest that instead of being overly enthusiastic in your search, be intentional: take your time to vet profiles and interact only with people you can genuinely see yourself dating. You may not even necessarily know what these profiles might have in common, but rest assured the algorithm will be at work in the background finding the common thread and refining its suggestions for you in the future.

Sources indicate that the default Hinge filters are very relaxed, but there's actually a Dealbreakers toggle hidden in the Dating Preferences section of your profile. The normal preferences (location and age range, for example) are taken into account but treated more like guidelines than hard limits. However, if you start enabling your Dealbreakers, Hinge will treat them as hard limits and never even show you profiles that don't match your preferences. As Hinge put it to us, "Hinge will only show you each other if you both meet the dealbreakers that either of you set, such as wanting kids. This helps you focus on people who feel like a real long-term match.".

Industry observers note that most dating app consumers, out of sheer eagerness to start browsing local singles, make a half-hearted attempt to fill out their profiles, usually doing the bare minimum to meet the app's requirements. But Hinge offers an extremely generous array of profile fields, and the more you fill out, the more data the algorithm can use to do its matchmaking work.

And as Hinge pointed out to us, not answering a question is treated like a negative, actively shrinking your dating pool: "When you select 'prefer not to say,' it limits who can see you. From family plans and dating intentions to drinking habits, you're excluded from being shown to people who've set Dealbreakers around those compatibility factors.".

We recommend you put particular focus on filling out Hinge's prompts in a thoughtful way, taking particular care to choose ones that reflect directly on your personality or interests.

In Hinge's own profile guide, they offer vital advice that is too often overlooked: ditch the clichés and one-word or low-effort responses, and take the time to give a personal answer to every question. And take the time to answer a voice prompt, as you'll be rewarded by the algorithm for doing so.

Finally, there's good evidence that Hinge's algorithm rewards profiles with refreshed photos, so if you haven't updated your main photos in a minute, follow their photo refresh guide to optimize your new pics.

If you follow the steps above, you should start to see the algorithm working more in your favor, and you'll look forward to each day's latest Most Compatible suggestion.

Don't be overwhelmed or waste an hour scrolling through your services to determine what to watch. We've got your back, whatever your mood. Mashable offers watch guides for all of the above, broken down by genre: comedy, thriller, horror, documentary, and animation, among others. But if you're seeking something brand new (or just new to streaming), we've got you covered there, too.

Recent findings suggest that apple TV's Way of the Warrior Kid focuses on struggling middle schooler Marc (Jude Hill), whose classmates bully him relentlessly. When his Navy SEAL uncle Jake (Chris Pratt) comes to spend the summer with him and his mom Sarah (Linda Cardellini), Marc will get a chance to learn how to defend himself.

To help his nephew, Jake puts together "Operation Warrior Kid." Based on Jake's own military training, his program is less about teaching Marc to fight, and more about teaching him to embrace true courage. Along the way, Jake will wrestle with demons of his own, as both he and Marc discover their own bravery.* — Belen Edwards, Entertainment Reporter.

Starring: Chris Pratt, Jude Hill, Linda Cardellini, Levi McConaughey, Ava Torres, Darien Sills-Evans, Carl McDowell, Parker Young.

How to watch: Way of the Warrior Kid is now streaming on Apple TV.

In 2010, Aaron Sorkin wrote The Social Network and David Fincher directed. For its sort-of sequel, The Social Reckoning, Sorkin writes and directs, while Jeremy Strong takes over the role of Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg from Jesse Eisenberg. And all of this means a finger-wagging film that's more frustrating than revealing.

Recent findings suggest that based on investigative reporter Jeff Horwitz's The Facebook Files, the film stars The Bear's Jeremy Allen White and Anora's Oscar-winning Mikey Madison as Horwitz and whistleblower Frances Haugen, respectively. But the title is a bit of a misnomer, because what reckoning?

Industry observers note that sorkin's political idealism is just one of his vexing indulgences, alongside his nostalgia for antiquated gender dynamics. In my review, I denounced The Social Reckoning as "misogynistic" and "unfunny," concluding, "Sorkin's dusty devices, problematic archetypes, and cringeworthy dialogue make the film feel instantly dated. Scroll on." — Kristy Puchko, Entertainment Editor.

Starring: Mikey Madison, Jeremy Allen White, Wunmi Mosaku, Betty Gilpin, Billy Magnussen, Bill Burr, and Jeremy Strong.

How to watch: The Social Reckoning is now available on digital.

Recent findings suggest that having been a Hollywood star for decades, Rob Lowe's filmography meets people in different eras, whether you saw his 1980s Brat Pack breakout roles in The Outsiders and St. Elmo's Fire, revered his '90s smarminess in Wayne's World, or followed him down 2000s West Wing and 2010s Parks and Recreation hallways.

According to recent reports, being an 18-year-old breakout star in '80s Tinseltown proved quite the start for Lowe, the focus of Netflix's new documentary directed by Chris Smith (Tiger King, Sr., Fyre). Featuring interviews with Lowe as well as famous friends like Gwyneth Paltrow and Demi Moore, the film focuses on Lowe's chaotic life in Hollywood, through ups, downs, scandal, and stardom. — Shannon Connellan, Senior Editor.

How to watch: Rob Lowe: The Outsider is now streaming on Netflix.

'Twas the night before Christmas, when all through the house, demons invaded, so GTFO. That's essentially the set-up for On the Last day of Christmas, Paramount+'s festive horror film written and directed by Kevin Arbouet. Set in an apartment in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, the film sees Queen Sugar's Tanyell Waivers as a mother whose yuletide celebrations with her teen son (Way of the Warrior Kid's Ellis Hobbs IV) are interrupted by sinister entities. — S.C.

Starring: Tanyell Waivers, Ellis Hobbs IV, David Jensen, and Brandon Gilpin.

Recent findings suggest that how to watch: On the Last Day of Christmas debuts on Paramount+ on Nov. 27.

The story of Karen Read began on Jan. 29, 2022, when her boyfriend John O'Keefe was found dead in the snow outside of the home of a friend. As a well-respected member of the Boston Police Department, O'Keefe was mourned by friends, family, and Boston as a whole. But when it came to how he died, two camps emerged.

One — including the Boston PD — alleged he was killed in a hit and run, by his girlfriend Karen Read, and left to die in the snow. The other — spurred on by a podcaster known as Turtleboy — alleged that Read was being framed by O'Keefe's colleagues in an elaborate cover-up. This three-part Netflix documentary series from Danielle Johnson Cutts delves into both theories through interviews with O'Keefe's family, friends, and the most notorious investigator attached to the case. However, while Cutts includes plenty of archival interviews, she does not have new interviews with Read or Turtleboy, who both declined to participate in the doc. Cutts' investigation is thoughtful, thorough, and balanced. But don't expect big twists like Netflix's Unknown Number or outrageous interviews like The Crash. — K.P.

How to watch: The Trials of Karen Read is now streaming on Netflix.

Here's a documentary you'll want to watch with the volume loud and proud.

Directed by Douglas Tirola, New Wave is a four-part documentary series delving into the rise of the eponymous music genre from 1977 to 1987 and beyond. Its music was bouncy, bizarre, and massively influential. To explore New Wave's past, present, and future, Tirola brings together a jaw-dropping lineup of musicians for interview. Look at the featuring list below, for all the reason you need to tune in and bliss out. — K.P.

Starring: Andy Bell (Erasure), Andy McCluskey (OMD), Annabella Lwin (Bow Wow Wow), Billy Idol, Bob Geldof (Boomtown Rats), Brian Ritchie (Violent Femmes), Brian Setzer (Stray Cats), Chris Frantz (Talking Heads, Tom Tom Club), Curt Smith (Tears for Fears), Danny Elfman (Oingo Boingo), Dave Wakeling (English Beat), Fred Schneider, Glenn Tilbrook (Squeeze), Jim Kerr (Simple Minds), John Taylor (Duran Duran), Johnny Marr (The Smiths), Kate Pierson (The B-52s), Kathy Valentine (The Go-Go's), Mark Goodman (MTV), Mark Mothersbaugh (Devo), Martha Davis (The Motels), Martha Quinn (MTV), Matt Pinfield (music journalist), Miles Copeland (IRS Records music executive), Richard Blade (DJ), Stewart Copeland (The Police), and Thomas Dolby.

How to watch: Upcoming Wave is now streaming on MGM+.

In a recent development, with Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan at the moment in U.S. jail fighting extradition to the UK on charges of rape and sex trafficking, Andrew Tate: Toxic Empire delves into the backstory of the manosphere influencer. Cutting between archive footage of the Tate brothers and interviews with people in his circle and alleged victims, the four-part series from director/producer team Julian Hobbs and Elli Hakami explores how the Tates made their money — and the allegations they're currently facing. — Sam Haysom, Editor, General Assignments.

How to watch: Andrew Tate: Toxic Empire is streaming on HBO Max, with new episodes on Wednesdays.

Sources indicate that enemies-to-lovers Christmas rom-com with a job cuts edge, anyone? Michelle Randolph and Chris Briney lead Prime Video's Clashing Through the Snow as publishing editors Hannah and Ryan, who are fighting over one career-saving contract (nothing like redundancies in media to celebrate the holidays, right?) — and they've got to make it to New York in time. So, of course they'll be snowed under at the airport! Of course they'll have to share one rental car to meet deadline! Of course there'll be small towns en route to the significant city to make them remember what Christmas is all about! Also, Paris Hilton and Julia Fox are in this, so there's something for everyone. — S.C.

Starring: Christopher Briney, Michelle Randolph, Lukas Gage, Paris Hilton, Julia Fox, and PJ Byrne.

How to watch: Clashing Through the Snow is now on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that emma Fogarty and Colin Farrell's longtime friendship fuels Rachel Fleit's lauded documentary, The Slightest Touch, streaming on HBO Max this week. Living with Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB), Fogarty's condition means her skin is extremely fragile and can easily blister. However, she's determined to run the Dublin Marathon for her 40th birthday with her movie star friend, raising awareness for EB together. It's this key cause that sees Farrell inviting cameras into his personal life too, as Fleit explores this powerful, lasting friendship as parallel portraits. — S.C.

Starring: Colin Farrell and Emma Fogarty.

How to watch: The Slightest Touch is now streaming on HBO Max.

Recent findings suggest that sesame Street is back with its 57th season! This timeless series is never to be taken for granted. Each episode brings family-friendly fun in the form of games, animation, original music, celebrity guests, and plenty of laughs with our favorite Sesame Street residents. This newly introduced volume (Volume 4 on Netflix) also promises more adventures with Elmo, Abby, and Tango. — K.P.

How to watch: Sesame Street, Season 57 is now playing on Netflix.

It has been revealed that A creepy Italian village filled with smiling locals and an angel in human form are the ingredients making up The Holy Boy, Paolo Strippoli's horror about a teacher (Michele Riondino) who moves house only to stumble across a bizarre local tradition: In order to take their pain and sadness away, the locals all take turns hugging 15-year-old Matteo (Giulio Feltri). Fans of religious horror with a side order of telekinetic power may want to mark this one in their calendars. — S.H.

Starring: Michele Riondino, Giulio Feltri, Paolo Pierobon, and Romana Maggiora Vergano.

How to watch: The Holy Boy debuts on Shudder on Nov. 27.

Following the Season 1 finale, Sophie (Brittany Snow) and Margo (Malin Åkerman) have gone from lovers to estranged enemies. However, it's not long before their secrets and some newly introduced common enemies bring them back together. As The Hunting Wives continues to weave its web of seduction and gun-slinging, will these two hunters make it out alive?* — B.E.

Starring: Brittany Snow, Malin Åkerman, Dermot Mulroney, Jaime Ray Newman, Evan Jonigkeit, George Ferrier, Karen Rodriguez, and Hunter Emery.

Industry observers note that how to watch: The Hunting Wives Season 2 premieres Nov. 26 on Netflix.

This is probably the most bonkers title on our list this week, so all hail Jennifer Lopez, a consummate entertainer.

Sources indicate that A recording of her Las Vegas residency, The JLo Show features the American pop icon singing her hits, including "Jenny from the Block" and "I'm Real." But there's so much more. Surrounded by back-up dancers and snatched in the tightest, most glittery nude illusion bodysuits, Lopez also covers classics like "Let Me Entertain You" and recreates one of her significant numbers from the bold musical bomb Kiss of the Spider-Woman. But that's still not all. Lopez also cracks jokes about her many marriages with an uncrackable face, and generally mythologizes herself through selected anecdotes. And that is still not all.

Performing numbers reminiscent of West Side Story and Chicago, JLo also lets Broadway know what they're missing. Much like her wild autobiographical visual album This is Me...Now, The JLo Show offers Lopez doing too much, and being absolutely dazzling all the while. — K.P.

How to watch: The JLo Show debuts on Paramount+ on Nov. 26.

Remember how Curtis "50 Cent" Jackson produced a doc about Diddy that made the public reconsider the 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur (among other things)? Well, if you binge-watched Netflix's Sean Combs: The Reckoning, we wager you're already seated for The Tupac Tapes with Angie Martinez.

Recent findings suggest that this one focuses on Radio Hall of Famer and New York Times bestselling author Angie Martinez, as she looks back on her taped interview with Shakur, recorded in his Los Angeles home months before his death. In this four-part video podcast, Martinez plays portions of the tapes never heard before by the public. Plus, she discusses Shakur's life, legacy, and death with guests like Charlamagne Tha God, Joe Budden, Big Boy, Dream Hampton, RZA, and Wallo. — K.P.

How to watch: The Tupac Tapes with Angie Martinez debuts on Netflix on Nov. 27.

In a recent development, it can be hard to get scientific research funded. And in writer-director Alex Goyette's horror Breeder, no one knows this better than MIT dropout Russell (Daniel Doheny). But it seems like his luck has changed when he finds an investor in Patti Kolb (Glee's Dot-Marie Jones), an affluent breeder of minature poodles. There's just one catch. She wants to meet him. In person. At her remote ranch. Where she's got a fleet of young women in residence.

As you might guess from this setup (or the trailer above), Kolb isn't only interested in breeding dogs. And her methods for studs that don't meet her expectations are...harsh. It's little wonder that this mean indie has been gathering praise all summer long as it hit the film festival circus. Now you can see what horror lovers have been barking about. — K.P.

Starring: Daniel Doheny, Dot-Marie Jones, Maddie Phillips, and Tanaya Beatty.

How to watch: Breeder is now available on digital.

Romanian filmmaker Cristian Mungiu was previously best known for his 2007 drama 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days. However, after winning the Palme d'Or at this year's Cannes Film Festival for Fjord, he's finding a latest international audience, with a little help from the MCU's Sebastian Stan.

Recent findings suggest that with a shaved head and bushy beard, Stan is unrecognizable from his role as the Winter Soldier. Opposite Norwegian film star Renate Reinsve (The Worst Person in the World, Sentimental Value), he plays a soft-spoken Romanian engineer, who's moved his wife and children to Norway to be closer to her family. But cultural differences hit hard, as the family's evangelical Christian devotion is seen as suffocating and even abusive by the children's teachers. When child protective services step in, Fjord becomes part family-drama, part crime-drama, inviting audiences to make their own decisions about right and wrong. — K.P.

Starring: Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve.

How to watch: Fjord is now available on digital.

Aside from holding titles from the World Boxing Council and the International Boxing Organization, British boxer Tyson Fury might be best known for his ferocity and endurance in the ring. However, his Netflix documentary, Tyson Fury, goes behind his tough exterior to reveal his tenderness.

Interviews with his fighter father John Fury reveal a trying childhood, as well as the shocking revelation that challenged Tyson's idea of his dad. Director Lucy Wilcox also interviews his wife, Paris Fury, who gives insights into the boxer as a supportive partner and loving father. Wilcox's approach to Tyson is compassionate, giving him space to be vulnerable as he talks about his trauma, his self-esteem concerns, and his struggles with suicidal ideation. And yet, she doesn't avoid touchy topics, like the public backlash over his comments about homosexuality and women. So, while this is an empathetic portrait of the fighter, it's also as hard-hitting as its subject. — K.P.

Starring: Tyson Fury, Paris Fury, and John Fury.

Industry observers note that how to watch: Tyson Fury debuts on Netflix on Nov. 27.

If you haven't had an entanglement with Wicker in regular unmoving cinemas or in rumbling 4DX, this is your chance to log it. Based on Ursula Wills-Jones' short story "The Wicker Husband," this raunchy, hilarious, heartwarming fairy tale sees a fisherwoman (Olivia Colman) requesting a basket weaver (Peter Dinklage) to literally make her a husband in order to spite the local townspeople (led by Elizabeth Debicki). And it works, with Alexander Skarsgård brought to life as a dashing wicker man.

"It's a deeply silly, fairy tale concept," I wrote in my review. "But what directors Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson have up their sleeve is a hilarious and heartfelt script, an incredibly talented cast, and magical production design...It's an artisanal Frankenstein tale, and one that will melt that brittle basket-woven heart of yours — or simply have you thinking about Taylor Swift's "Wood" differently." — S.C.

Starring: Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård, Peter Dinklage, and Elizabeth Debicki.

How to watch: Wicker is now available on digital.

Amy Poehler reunites with Parks and Recreation co-creator Mike Schur for Dig, a charming sitcom based on Kate Myers's novel Excavations. Poehler plays Elise, lead archaeologist on a Grecian archaeological dig. When she makes the discovery of a lifetime, she'll team up with a crew of fellow passionate archaeologists to uncover it in secret, far from the prying eyes of egotistical dig head Neville (Hugh Laurie).

While not always laugh-out-loud funny, Dig is a perfect warm and cozy watch, not to mention a wonderful character study of its wonderful core ensemble, made up of Poehler, Laurie, Geraldine Viswanathan, Antonia Thomas, and Fina Strazza. As I wrote in my review, "despite the flashy location and a latest mystery twist, Dig retains the core formula that made Parks and Recreation so irresistible: investing deeply in a lovable new crew of unlikely friends." — B.E.

Starring: Amy Poehler, Hugh Laurie, Geraldine Viswanathan, Antonia Thomas, and Fina Strazza.

How to watch: Dig premieres Nov. 23 on Peacock, with new episodes on Mondays.

You've never seen Blade Runner like you will in Blade Runner 2099. The TV series upends the hierarchy of the prior Blade Runner films entirely. Following a brutal uprising, replicants are now in control of humanity. Now, replicant blade runners are in charge of hunting rogue humans — among these is Cora (Hunter Schafer). Tired of running, she undertakes a dangerous mission that forces her to pose as a blade runner. She'll soon cross paths with blade runner Olwen (Michelle Yeoh), a replicant with only days left to live. In those final days, she and Cora will search for a group of runaway replicants on the hunt for a secret that can change the world.

Industry observers note that yeoh and Schafer are a match made in heaven, each handling Blade Runner 2099's action with eternal cool. Their unofficial third co-star is the world around them, brought to brilliant life by the production team. Imposing pyramids and seedy shops shine under neon lighting and threatening dust clouds, while Vangelis-esque synths usher us into a sense of cyberpunk noir. It's a towering technical achievement fronted by two exceptional leads, and a worthy addition to the Blade Runner franchise. — B.E.

Starring: Michelle Yeoh, Hunter Schafer, Dimitri Abold, Lewis Gribben, Katelyn Rose Downey, Daniel Rigby, Johnny Harris, Amy Lennox, Sheila Atim, Matthew Needham, Tom Burke, and Maurizio Lombardi.

Sources indicate that how to watch: Blade Runner 2099 premieres Nov. 25 on Prime Video.

Arguably the most talked-about movie of the year has landed on digital. And you better believe that's going to mean a fresh round of memes, spoofs, debates, and obsession.

Recent findings suggest that when the teaser for You Can See Everything first hit, it seemed like a joke. Canadian comedian Nathan Fielder — of all people — interviewing notorious Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes in her home, ahead of her prison sentence? How could that be a real movie? The critics were raving (me included). But audiences did too, taking this A24 doc to record-breaking heights, and turning Holmes and her romantic partner Billy Evans into a national conversation. It's buzz has even reached space.

Recent findings suggest that we're still saying the best way to see You Can See Everything is in theaters. But we're also giddy at the chance to be able to pause, rewind, and geek out with friends on a whole upcoming level now that we have the remote. — K.P.

Starring: Nathan Fielder, Elizabeth Holmes, and Billy Evans.

How to watch: You Can See Everything is available for purchase on Prime Video.
